at male.explanation: "At male" means "to paint": Han maler væggen hvid (He paints the wall white). It also works for pictures: Hun maler et billede (She paints a picture). For drawing with a pencil, use at tegne (to draw).

sentence.da: Vi vil **male** huset gult.
sentence.en: We want to paint the house yellow.

at mangle.explanation: "At mangle" means "to lack" or "to be missing". What is missing comes after it: Jeg mangler en pen (I am missing a pen). Der mangler en stol (A chair is missing).

sentence.da: Børn må ikke **mangle** mad og tøj.
sentence.en: Children must not lack food and clothes.

at manipulere.explanation: "At manipulere" means "to manipulate", to influence someone or something in a hidden or unfair way. It can also mean to handle or change data on purpose: at manipulere tal (to manipulate numbers).

sentence.da: Reklamer kan **manipulere** børn til at ønske sig legetøj.
sentence.en: Ads can manipulate children into wanting toys.

at markere.explanation: "At markere" means "to mark", to make something visible or to show that it is there. It is used for a line on paper, text on a screen or an event: at markere en fødselsdag (to mark a birthday).

sentence.da: Du skal **markere** det vigtigste med en gul tusch.
sentence.en: You must mark the most important part with a yellow felt-tip pen.

at mase.explanation: "At mase" means "to squeeze / push", to force your way forward or into a tight space, often in a crowd. It is a pushy movement with your body: Han masede sig forbi mig (He pushed past me).

sentence.da: Folk begyndte at **mase**, da dørene åbnede.
sentence.en: People began to push when the doors opened.

at massere.explanation: "At massere" means "to massage", to rub and press muscles to ease them. You can massage a person or a body part: at massere nakken (to massage the neck).

sentence.da: Han kan **massere** mine skuldre, når de gør ondt.
sentence.en: He can massage my shoulders when they hurt.

at meddele.explanation: "At meddele" means "to announce / inform", to tell something officially. It is the word for official news: Vi meddeler, at kontoret er lukket (We announce that the office is closed).

sentence.da: Banken vil **meddele** kunderne de nye priser i morgen.
sentence.en: The bank will inform the customers of the new prices tomorrow.

at medføre.explanation: "At medføre" means "to lead to / result in", to have something follow from it: Regnen medfører oversvømmelser (The rain results in floods).

forms.en: it has led to / resulted in

sentence.da: Det nye system kan **medføre** store besparelser for firmaet.
sentence.en: The new system can lead to big savings for the company.

at meditere.explanation: "At meditere" means "to meditate", to sit quietly and calm your mind.

sentence.da: Hun vil **meditere** i stilhed for at slappe af.
sentence.en: She wants to meditate in silence to relax.

at medvirke.explanation: "At medvirke" means "to contribute / take part", to be one of the people involved in something, such as a film, a play or a result. It is often followed by i (in): at medvirke i en undersøgelse (to take part in a study).

sentence.da: Flere kendte skuespillere vil **medvirke** i filmen.
sentence.en: Several famous actors will take part in the film.

at melde.explanation: "At melde" means "to report / announce", to say or notify something. It has many small uses, for example at melde sig til (to sign up for) and at melde fra (to say that you cannot come).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **melde** mig syg på arbejdet i morgen.
sentence.en: I have to call in sick at work tomorrow.

at melde afbud.explanation: "At melde afbud" means "to cancel", when you tell people you cannot come: Han meldte afbud til festen (He told them he could not come to the party). To cancel the event itself, use at aflyse (to cancel).

sentence.da: Jeg må desværre **melde afbud** til mødet.
sentence.en: Unfortunately, I have to tell them I cannot come to the meeting.

at melde sig.explanation: "At melde sig" means "to sign up", and also "to volunteer": Jeg meldte mig til kurset (I signed up for the course). Hvem vil melde sig? (Who will volunteer?)

sentence.da: Man kan **melde sig** på listen ved døren.
sentence.en: You can sign up on the list by the door.

at melde sig syg.explanation: "At melde sig syg" means "to call in sick", that is, to tell your work or school that you are ill and cannot come. It is about the act of reporting, not the illness itself: Jeg er syg (I am sick) just says how you feel.

sentence.da: Han har feber og må **melde sig syg**.
sentence.en: He has a fever and has to call in sick.

at melde sig til.explanation: "At melde sig til" means "to sign up for" a course, a team or an event. What you join comes after til: Jeg melder mig til kurset (I sign up for the course).

sentence.da: Hun vil **melde sig til** fodboldholdet i år.
sentence.en: She wants to sign up for the soccer team this year.

at melde til politiet.explanation: "At melde til politiet" means "to report to the police". Use it when you tell the police about something that happened, such as a theft or an accident: Han meldte det til politiet (He reported it to the police).

forms.en: I have reported to the police

sentence.da: Når man bliver bestjålet, bør man **melde til politiet**.
sentence.en: When you are robbed, you should report to the police.

at mene.explanation: "At mene" means "to mean / think": you hold an opinion. Jeg mener, at du har ret means "I believe you are right". Hvad mener du? means "What do you mean?". At synes (to think) is for feelings and taste: Jeg synes, at maden er god (I think the food is good). For the meaning of a word, Danish uses at betyde (to mean).

sentence.da: Du må gerne **mene** noget andet.
sentence.en: You are welcome to think something else.

at mime.explanation: "At mime" means "to mime", to act something out with your body and no words. It is also used for a singer who moves the lips to recorded sound: Sangeren mimer (The singer lip-syncs).

sentence.da: Hun kan **mime** en hel historie uden at sige noget.
sentence.en: She can mime a whole story without saying anything.

at minde om.explanation: "At minde om" means "to remind of", and also "to resemble": Du minder mig om min bror (You remind me of my brother). To remind someone to do something, add at (to): Jeg minder dig om at ringe (I remind you to call).

sentence.da: Den sang kan **minde om** sommeren.
sentence.en: That song can be reminiscent of summer.

at mindes.explanation: "At mindes" means "to remember / commemorate", to think back on someone or something, often with warmth. It is used for people and events from the past: Vi mindes vores bedstefar (We remember our grandfather). For facts and things to do, use at huske (to remember): Jeg husker dit navn (I remember your name).

sentence.da: Vi vil **mindes** dem, der døde i krigen.
sentence.en: We want to remember those who died in the war.

at mindske.explanation: "At mindske" means "to reduce", to make an amount, a risk or a problem go down: at mindske risikoen (to reduce the risk).

sentence.da: Man kan **mindske** forbruget ved at slukke lyset.
sentence.en: You can reduce consumption by turning off the light.

at misforstå.explanation: "At misforstå" means "to misunderstand". It is built from mis- (wrongly) and at forstå (to understand), and mis- also starts at misbruge (to misuse).

sentence.da: Jeg kan nemt **misforstå** dig på telefonen.
sentence.en: I can easily misunderstand you on the phone.

at mislykkes.explanation: "At mislykkes" means "to fail", when a try does not work out. The thing fails, not the person: Forsøget mislykkedes (The attempt failed). For a person who fails a test, use at dumpe (to flunk).

sentence.da: Hvis planen **mislykkes**, må vi prøve noget andet.
sentence.en: If the plan fails, we must try something else.

at misse.explanation: "At misse" means "to miss", when you are too late for something: Vi missede toget (We missed the train). Missing a person is at savne (to miss): Jeg savner dig (I miss you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **misse** bussen i morgen tidlig.
sentence.en: I don't want to miss the bus tomorrow morning.

at miste.explanation: "At miste" means "to lose" something you had: Jeg mistede min nøgle (I lost my key). It also fits people: Hun mistede sin bedstefar (She lost her grandfather). To lose a game is at tabe: Vi tabte kampen (We lost the match).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **miste** min telefon igen.
sentence.en: I don't want to lose my phone again.

at mistænke.explanation: "At mistænke" means "to suspect", to think that someone has done something wrong, without being sure. The thing they are suspected of comes after for (of): Hvem mistænker du for det? (Who do you suspect of it?)

sentence.da: Politiet kan **mistænke** en nabo for tyveriet.
sentence.en: The police may suspect a neighbor of the theft.

at mjave.explanation: "At mjave" means "to meow", the sound a cat makes: Katten mjaver, fordi den er sulten (The cat meows because it is hungry). Purring is at spinde: Katten spinder (The cat purrs).

sentence.da: Jeg kan høre katten **mjave** udenfor.
sentence.en: I can hear the cat meow outside.

at modarbejde.explanation: "At modarbejde" means "to counteract", and says that someone works against a person or a plan on purpose: Han modarbejder mig på jobbet (He works against me at work). For something that weakens an effect, such as a medicine, use at modvirke (to counteract an effect).

sentence.da: Nogle kolleger prøver at **modarbejde** den nye chef.
sentence.en: Some colleagues try to work against the new boss.

at modbevise.explanation: "At modbevise" means "to disprove": to show with facts that a statement is wrong, as in modbevise en teori (disprove a theory). It starts with mod (against), the same mod as in at modsige (to contradict).

sentence.da: Et godt alibi kan **modbevise**, at man var der.
sentence.en: A good alibi can disprove that you were there.

at moderere.explanation: "At moderere" means "to moderate", to make something less extreme or less strong. It is also used for someone who leads a discussion, often online: Hun modererer debatten (She moderates the debate).

sentence.da: Du bør **moderere** dit sprog, når børnene hører på.
sentence.en: You should tone down your language when the children are listening.

at modsige.explanation: "At modsige" means "to contradict": to say or show the opposite of what someone or something else says: Det modsiger, hvad du sagde før (That contradicts what you said before). With sig selv it means to contradict yourself: Du modsiger dig selv (You contradict yourself).

sentence.da: Optagelserne kan **modsige** vidnets forklaring.
sentence.en: The recordings can contradict the witness's explanation.

at modstille.explanation: "At modstille" means "to contrast": to put two things next to each other so you can see how they are unlike: modstille by og land (contrast city and country).

sentence.da: Artiklen vil **modstille** to meget forskellige syn på skolen.
sentence.en: The article wants to contrast two very different views of the school.

at modstå.explanation: "At modstå" means "to resist", to hold out against something, such as a temptation, an attack or a strong force. The past is irregular: jeg modstod (I resisted).

sentence.da: Jeg kan aldrig **modstå** en frisk kage.
sentence.en: I can never resist a fresh cake.

at modtage.explanation: "At modtage" means "to receive": Jeg har modtaget din mail (I have received your email). It sounds a bit formal. In everyday speech, Danes often say at få (to get): Jeg fik en gave (I got a gift).

sentence.da: Vi skal **modtage** en pakke i morgen.
sentence.en: We are going to receive a package tomorrow.

at modvirke.explanation: "At modvirke" means "to counteract": to work against an effect or a development so it gets weaker: Motion kan modvirke stress (Exercise can counteract stress). When a person works against your plans, use at modarbejde (to work against).

sentence.da: Sund mad kan **modvirke** træthed hen på dagen.
sentence.en: Healthy food can counteract tiredness later in the day.

at more sig.explanation: "At more sig" means "to have fun", and sig changes with the person: Vi morer os (We are having fun).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **more sig** til festen.
sentence.en: The children are going to have fun at the party.

at motionere.explanation: "At motionere" means "to exercise" for your body, for example by walking or swimming: Jeg motionerer tre gange om ugen (I exercise three times a week). The thing itself is motion (exercise): Motion er godt for dig (Exercise is good for you).

sentence.da: Lægen siger, at jeg skal **motionere** mere.
sentence.en: The doctor says that I should exercise more.

at motivere.explanation: "At motivere" means "to motivate", to give someone a reason or a wish to do something. You can motivate another person or yourself: Jeg motiverer mig selv (I motivate myself).

sentence.da: En god leder kan **motivere** hele holdet.
sentence.en: A good leader can motivate the whole team.

at mumle.explanation: "At mumle" means "to mumble", to speak so quietly or unclearly that it is hard to hear: Han mumlede noget, jeg ikke forstod (He mumbled something I did not understand).

sentence.da: Han begyndte at **mumle**, så ingen kunne forstå ham.
sentence.en: He started to mumble, so no one could understand him.

at myrde.explanation: "At myrde" means "to murder", to kill a person on purpose. It is stronger than at dræbe (to kill), which can also be an accident.

sentence.da: Han blev dømt for at **myrde** sin nabo.
sentence.en: He was convicted of murdering his neighbor.

at måle.explanation: "At måle" means "to measure", finding out the size or amount of something: Jeg måler bordet (I am measuring the table). It works for temperature too: Lægen måler min temperatur (The doctor is taking my temperature).

sentence.da: Man kan **måle** længden med en lineal.
sentence.en: You can measure the length with a ruler.

at måtte.explanation: "At måtte" means "may / must": it covers being allowed to and having to. Må jeg gå? means "May I go?", while Jeg må gå nu means "I have to go now". Du må ikke means "You must not", a strong warning. Another action word follows straight after it, with no at.

forms.en: I was allowed to / had to

sentence.da: Vi kommer til at **måtte** vente en time.
sentence.en: We will have to wait an hour.

at mærke.explanation: "At mærke" means "to feel" something physical, and also "to notice": Jeg mærker regnen (I feel the rain). Han mærkede ikke noget (He did not notice anything).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **mærke** vinden i mit ansigt.
sentence.en: I can feel the wind on my face.

at mætte.explanation: "At mætte" means "to fill (up) / satisfy", to take away hunger so that you want no more. It is used for food: Havregrød mætter godt (Oatmeal fills you up well).

sentence.da: En stor portion pasta kan **mætte** hele familien.
sentence.en: A large portion of pasta can fill up the whole family.

at møde op.explanation: "At møde op" means "to show up", to come where you are expected: Han mødte op til tiden (He showed up on time). It is often said about people who do not: Hun mødte ikke op (She did not show up).

sentence.da: Alle skal **møde op** klokken otte.
sentence.en: Everyone has to show up at eight o'clock.

at mødes.explanation: "At mødes" means "to meet each other", usually by plan: Vi mødes i morgen (We meet tomorrow). Without the s, at møde means "to meet" someone: Jeg møder Anna (I meet Anna).

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **mødes** på cafeen i morgen.
sentence.en: We would like to meet at the cafe tomorrow.

en madallergi.explanation: "En madallergi" means "a food allergy", when your body reacts badly to a certain food, such as milk or fish. The first part is mad, the Danish word for food. It starts many words, like madpakke (a packed lunch).

sentence.da: Min søn har en **madallergi** og kan ikke spise æg.
sentence.en: My son has a food allergy and cannot eat eggs.

en madanmelder.explanation: "En madanmelder" means "a food critic", a person who writes about restaurants and meals in newspapers or online. The second part, anmelder (critic), is used in other fields too: en filmanmelder (a film critic).

sentence.da: Vores **madanmelder** gav restauranten fem stjerner i avisen.
sentence.en: Our food critic gave the restaurant five stars in the paper.

en madding.explanation: "En madding" means "a bait", something used to attract fish so they bite. It is built from mad (food).

sentence.da: Ormen er en god **madding**, når man fisker efter ørred.
sentence.en: The worm is good bait when you fish for trout.

en madkasse.explanation: "En madkasse" means "a lunch box", the box you bring food in to school or work.

sentence.da: Min søn tager sin **madkasse** med i skole.
sentence.en: My son takes his lunch box to school.

en madkultur.explanation: "En madkultur" means "a food culture", the way people in a country or place cook, eat and think about food. Danish madkultur is known for smørrebrød (open sandwiches).

sentence.da: I Danmark er rugbrød en vigtig del af vores **madkultur**.
sentence.en: In Denmark rye bread is an important part of our food culture.

en madordning.explanation: "En madordning" means "a meal program", an arrangement where meals are served to children, for example in a daycare, usually for a fee. It is built from mad (food) and ordning (arrangement).

sentence.da: Børnehaven har en **madordning** med frokost hver dag.
sentence.en: The kindergarten has a meal program with lunch every day.

en madpakke.explanation: "En madpakke" means "a packed lunch", usually sandwiches you make at home and take to school or work.

sentence.da: Jeg tager min **madpakke** med på arbejde.
sentence.en: I take my packed lunch to work.

en madplan.explanation: "En madplan" means "a meal plan", a list of what you will cook and eat on each day of the week. Many people make one before they go shopping, so they buy only what they need.

sentence.da: Vi laver en **madplan** hver søndag og køber ind til hele ugen.
sentence.en: We make a meal plan every Sunday and shop for the whole week.

en madras.explanation: "En madras" means "a mattress", the thick pad you lie on at night.

sentence.da: Jeg sover bedre på en blød **madras**.
sentence.en: I sleep better on a soft mattress.

en madrest.explanation: "En madrest" means "a food scrap", a small bit of food left over after cooking or eating. The plural madrester often means the leftovers from a whole meal.

sentence.da: Der er kun en lille **madrest** tilbage på tallerkenen.
sentence.en: There is only a small food scrap left on the plate.

en madvare.explanation: "En madvare" means "a food product", something sold for people to eat, such as bread, cheese or canned fish. The matching word for things to drink is drikkevarer (drinks).

sentence.da: Mælk er en **madvare**, og den skal stå i køleskabet.
sentence.en: Milk is a food product, and it has to be kept in the fridge.

en madvogn.explanation: "En madvogn" means "a food truck", a vehicle that sells cooked food on the street or at festivals. The second part, vogn, means a cart or wagon on wheels: en barnevogn (a stroller) uses the same word.

sentence.da: Ved festivalen står der en **madvogn** med burgere og pommes frites.
sentence.en: At the festival there is a food truck with burgers and fries.

en mafia.explanation: "En mafia" means "a mafia", an organized criminal group. The word is used for the Italian Mafia and for similar groups.

sentence.da: Filmen handler om en **mafia** i New York.
sentence.en: The movie is about a mafia in New York.

en magt.explanation: "En magt" means "a power", the ability to decide things and control others, such as the power of a government or a boss. For electric power, use strøm: Strømmen er gået (The power is out).

sentence.da: Politikere har **magt**, fordi vi stemmer på dem.
sentence.en: Politicians have power because we vote for them.

en mail.explanation: "En mail" means "an email". It is the short everyday word for en e-mail (an email).

sentence.da: Jeg sender dig en **mail** i dag.
sentence.en: I am sending you an email today.

en majestæt.explanation: "En majestæt" means "a majesty", the title for a king or queen. You address a ruler as Deres Majestæt (Your Majesty).

sentence.da: Man siger **majestæt**, når man taler til kongen.
sentence.en: You say Majesty when you talk to the king.

en major.explanation: "En major" means "a major", an officer rank in the military. It is only a rank: for important or serious, Danish does not use major but vigtig (important) or alvorlig (serious).

sentence.da: En **major** er højere i rang end en kaptajn.
sentence.en: A major is higher in rank than a captain.

en makrel.explanation: "En makrel" means "a mackerel", a fish that is eaten a lot in Denmark, often smoked, or from a can as makrel i tomat (mackerel in tomato sauce).

sentence.da: En **makrel** har striber på ryggen og lever i havet.
sentence.en: A mackerel has stripes on its back and lives in the sea.

en maler.explanation: "En maler" means "a painter", both an artist and someone who paints walls: En maler maler vores køkken (A painter is painting our kitchen). The situation shows which one is meant.

sentence.da: Min bror er **maler** og maler huse.
sentence.en: My brother is a painter and paints houses.

en manager.explanation: "En manager" means "a manager", an English loan word for a person who looks after a team or an artist's career. For a boss at an ordinary workplace, Danes more often say chef (boss).

sentence.da: Sangerens **manager** ordner alle koncerter og aftaler.
sentence.en: The singer's manager arranges all the concerts and deals.

en manchetknap.explanation: "En manchetknap" means "a cufflink", a small decorative fastener that closes the ends of the sleeves on a dress shirt. Men wear them mostly with formal clothes at special events.

sentence.da: Han lukker skjortens ærme med en **manchetknap** af sølv.
sentence.en: He closes the shirt sleeve with a silver cufflink.

en mand.explanation: "En mand" means "a man" or "a husband". With min (my) it means husband: min mand is my husband.

sentence.da: Min **mand** og jeg har to børn.
sentence.en: My husband and I have two children.

en mandel.explanation: "En mandel" means "an almond", often used in cakes and sweets. It also means a tonsil: Han fik fjernet mandlerne (He had his tonsils removed).

sentence.da: Marcipan er lavet af **mandel** og sukker.
sentence.en: Marzipan is made of almond and sugar.

en mangel.explanation: "En mangel" means "a shortage", when there is too little of something. It can also mean a defect in something you bought: Varen har en mangel (The item has a defect).

sentence.da: Der er **mangel** på sygeplejersker i mange lande.
sentence.en: There is a shortage of nurses in many countries.

en mango.explanation: "En mango" means "a mango", a sweet tropical fruit with a big pit.

sentence.da: En **mango** er gul og blød indeni.
sentence.en: A mango is yellow and soft inside.

en manke.explanation: "En manke" means "a mane", the long thick hair along the neck of a horse or around the head of a lion.

sentence.da: Hesten har en lang, sort **manke** på halsen.
sentence.en: The horse has a long, black mane on its neck.

en mappe.explanation: "En mappe" means "a folder", on a computer or for papers.

sentence.da: Jeg lægger alle billederne i en ny **mappe**.
sentence.en: I put all the pictures in a new folder.

en mariehøne.explanation: "En mariehøne" means "a ladybug", a small round beetle that eats insects harming plants. Literally the word is Marie plus høne (a hen), but it is not a bird.

sentence.da: En rød **mariehøne** har sorte prikker på ryggen.
sentence.en: A red ladybug has black dots on its back.

en mark.explanation: "En mark" means "a field", farmland where crops grow. Do not mix it up with et marked (a market).

sentence.da: Bonden kører en traktor ud på sin **mark**.
sentence.en: The farmer drives a tractor out onto his field.

en markedsandel.explanation: "En markedsandel" means "a market share", the part of all sales in a line of business that one company has. It is usually given in percent.

sentence.da: Firmaet har en **markedsandel** på tyve procent i Danmark.
sentence.en: The company has a market share of twenty percent in Denmark.

en markedsbod.explanation: "En markedsbod" means "a market stall", a small booth where someone shows goods at a market. It is built from marked (market) and bod (stall). On its own, en bod can also be a small storage room in an apartment building.

sentence.da: Jeg køber friske æbler i en **markedsbod**.
sentence.en: I buy fresh apples at a market stall.

en markering.explanation: "En markering" means "a marking", a painted stripe or symbol that shows something. It also means a public show of opinion or support, for example a minute of silence.

sentence.da: Cykelstien er vist med en hvid **markering** på vejen.
sentence.en: The bike path is shown with a white marking on the road.

en marketingchef.explanation: "En marketingchef" means "a marketing manager", the person in charge of a company's advertising and sales plans. Chef (boss, head) ends many job titles in Danish.

sentence.da: Vores **marketingchef** planlægger reklamerne til næste år.
sentence.en: Our marketing manager plans the ads for next year.

en mascara.explanation: "En mascara" means "a mascara", makeup that darkens your lashes. To put it on, say at tage mascara på (to put on mascara).

sentence.da: Med **mascara** bliver mine øjenvipper mørke.
sentence.en: With mascara my eyelashes get dark.

en maske.explanation: "En maske" means "a mask", something you wear to hide or protect part of your head. To put one on, say at tage en maske på (to put on a mask).

sentence.da: Lægen har en **maske** over munden.
sentence.en: The doctor has a mask over his mouth.

en maskine.explanation: "En maskine" means "a machine", something with moving parts that does work for you. It is the last part of words like en vaskemaskine (a washing machine).

sentence.da: Den nye **maskine** er hurtig, men larmer meget.
sentence.en: The new machine is fast but makes a lot of noise.

en massage.explanation: "En massage" means "a massage", pressing and rubbing the muscles to ease pain or tension. Danes often leave out en after få (to get): Jeg fik massage (I got a massage).

sentence.da: En time **massage** hjælper, når ryggen er spændt.
sentence.en: An hour of massage helps when the back is tense.

en masse.explanation: "En masse" means "a lot": en masse penge (a lot of money). Unlike English, it has no af (of) in between.

sentence.da: Der var en **masse** mennesker i byen.
sentence.en: There were a lot of people in town.

en matematiker.explanation: "En matematiker" means "a mathematician", someone who works with or studies mathematics. The ending -iker names a person in many fields: en fysiker (a physicist), en kemiker (a chemist).

sentence.da: En **matematiker** bruger tal og logik til at løse svære problemer.
sentence.en: A mathematician uses numbers and logic to solve hard problems.

en mave.explanation: "En mave" means "a stomach" or "a belly", the part of your body where food goes. To say it hurts, use ondt i maven (a pain in the stomach). Han har en stor mave (He has a big belly).

sentence.da: Maden går ned i din **mave**.
sentence.en: The food goes down into your stomach.

en mavebøjning.explanation: "En mavebøjning" means "a sit-up", a move that trains the stomach muscles. The second part comes from at bøje (to bend), as in en armbøjning (a push-up).

sentence.da: Man ligger på ryggen og løfter overkroppen i en **mavebøjning**.
sentence.en: You lie on your back and lift your upper body in a sit-up.

en mavepine.explanation: "En mavepine" means "a stomachache", built from mave (stomach) and pine (ache). Jeg har ondt i maven (My stomach hurts) means nearly the same.

sentence.da: Jeg har **mavepine** og vil ikke spise.
sentence.en: I have a stomachache and don't want to eat.

en mavesæk.explanation: "En mavesæk" means "a stomach (organ)", the bag inside your body where food is broken down. Mave alone can also mean the belly on the outside, so mavesæk is the clearer word for the organ itself.

sentence.da: Når du sluger maden, ender den i din **mavesæk**.
sentence.en: When you swallow the food, it ends up in your stomach.

en medalje.explanation: "En medalje" means "a medal", a prize for winning. Put the metal first to name it: en sølvmedalje (a silver medal).

sentence.da: Min datter vandt en **medalje** i svømning.
sentence.en: My daughter won a medal in swimming.

en medarbejder.explanation: "En medarbejder" means "an employee", a person who works for a company. It is built from med (with) and arbejder (worker), so it means someone who works with you. Med- also means fellow in en medstuderende (a fellow student) and en medspiller (a fellow player).

sentence.da: Vores nye **medarbejder** starter på mandag.
sentence.en: Our new employee starts on Monday.

en medborgerskabsprøve.explanation: "En medborgerskabsprøve" means "a civics test", a test about Danish society, history and culture, taken by people from abroad who want to stay in Denmark. It is built from medborgerskab (citizenship) and prøve (test).

sentence.da: Hun skal bestå en **medborgerskabsprøve** om dansk historie og samfund.
sentence.en: She must pass a civics test about Danish history and society.

en meddelelse.explanation: "En meddelelse" means "an announcement", a short official statement that tells people something. A message to a friend is called something else; meddelelse is for news from a school, a company or an authority.

sentence.da: Skolen sendte en **meddelelse** om den nye fridag.
sentence.en: The school sent an announcement about the new day off.

en medisterpølse.explanation: "En medisterpølse" means "a Danish pork sausage", a thick sausage of minced pork and spices that is usually fried. It is built from medister (spiced minced pork) and pølse (sausage).

sentence.da: Til aftensmad steger vi en **medisterpølse** med kartofler.
sentence.en: For dinner we fry a medister sausage with potatoes.

en meditation.explanation: "En meditation" means "a meditation", a quiet practice where you sit still and focus your mind on one thing, often your breathing.

sentence.da: Under en **meditation** sidder man stille og tænker på sin vejrtrækning.
sentence.en: During a meditation you sit still and think about your breathing.

en medspiller.explanation: "En medspiller" means "a teammate", someone who plays on the same side as you. Med means with, but mod means against, so en modspiller (an opponent) is the reverse.

sentence.da: En god **medspiller** hjælper de andre på holdet.
sentence.en: A good teammate helps the others on the team.

en mejetærsker.explanation: "En mejetærsker" means "a combine harvester", a large farm machine. The word is built from meje (to reap) and tærske (to thresh), the two jobs it does in one go: cutting the grain and separating the seeds.

sentence.da: Landmanden bruger en **mejetærsker**, når kornet er modent.
sentence.en: The farmer uses a combine harvester when the grain is ripe.

en mekaniker.explanation: "En mekaniker" means "a mechanic", a person who repairs cars and other machines for a living. It is the second half of longer words: en cykelmekaniker (a bike mechanic).

sentence.da: En **mekaniker** reparerer biler og motorer.
sentence.en: A mechanic repairs cars and engines.

en mellemlanding.explanation: "En mellemlanding" means "a layover", a short stop on the way to the final place. It is built from mellem (between) and landing (landing). Mellem is also in et mellemmåltid (a snack between meals).

sentence.da: På turen til Thailand har vi en **mellemlanding** i Dubai.
sentence.en: On the trip to Thailand, we have a layover in Dubai.

en melodi.explanation: "En melodi" means "a melody", the tune you sing or play. To hum it, say at nynne (to hum): Han nynner en melodi (He hums a tune).

sentence.da: Jeg kender den smukke **melodi**, men ikke teksten.
sentence.en: I know the beautiful melody, but not the lyrics.

en melon.explanation: "En melon" means "a melon", a big round fruit with a thick skin and soft, juicy flesh. Other kinds add a word in front, like en honningmelon (a honeydew melon).

sentence.da: En **melon** er stor, rund og sød indeni.
sentence.en: A melon is big, round and sweet inside.

en mening.explanation: "En mening" means "an opinion". It also means "sense": Det giver ingen mening (That makes no sense).

sentence.da: Jeg har en anden **mening** end dig.
sentence.en: I have a different opinion than you.

en meningsmåling.explanation: "En meningsmåling" means "an opinion poll", a way of finding out what people think, usually about politics. A small group is asked, and the answers are taken to show what the whole country thinks.

sentence.da: Ifølge en ny **meningsmåling** er flere unge utilfredse.
sentence.en: According to a new opinion poll, more young people are unhappy.

en mentor.explanation: "En mentor" means "a mentor", an experienced person who guides someone newer, often at work. A mentor usually helps one person over a long time, without a class or a set course.

sentence.da: En **mentor** hjælper en nyansat med at lære jobbet.
sentence.en: A mentor helps a new employee learn the job.

en menu.explanation: "En menu" means "a menu", the list of food at a restaurant. Dagens menu (the menu of the day) is a set meal chosen for that day.

sentence.da: Vi får en **menu** og vælger mad.
sentence.en: We get a menu and choose food.

en mester.explanation: "En mester" means "a champion" and also "a master". A trained craftsman is called mester too: en tømrermester (a master carpenter).

sentence.da: Min bror er **mester** i skak.
sentence.en: My brother is a chess champion.

en meter.explanation: "En meter" means "a meter". It stays meter after a number: to meter (two meters).

sentence.da: Han er over to **meter** høj.
sentence.en: He is over two meters tall.

en metode.explanation: "En metode" means "a method", a set way of doing something step by step. It is used for work and for study: en ny metode til at lære sprog (a new method for learning languages).

sentence.da: En **metode** er en bestemt måde at løse en opgave på.
sentence.en: A method is a certain way of solving a task.

en metro.explanation: "En metro" means "a metro", the underground train. You travel med metroen (by metro). Do not mix it up with S-tog (the S-train), which is a different train line.

sentence.da: Jeg kører med **metro** under jorden.
sentence.en: I ride the metro underground.

en middag.explanation: "En middag" means "a dinner", the main hot meal, eaten in the evening. It can also mean "noon", but the meal in the middle of the day is frokost (lunch).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **middag** klokken seks om aftenen.
sentence.en: We eat dinner at six in the evening.

en middagslur.explanation: "En middagslur" means "a nap", a short sleep in the middle of the day, not at night. It is built from middag (midday) and lur (a nap), and en lur alone works at any time of day.

sentence.da: Små børn tager ofte en **middagslur** efter frokost.
sentence.en: Small children often take a nap after lunch.

en midtergang.explanation: "En midtergang" means "an aisle", the walkway you go along on a plane, bus or train. It is built from midt (middle) and gang (hallway). The same gang is in a house: Skoene står i gangen (The shoes are in the hallway).

sentence.da: Han går ned ad en lang **midtergang** i flyet.
sentence.en: He walks down a long aisle in the plane.

en migræne.explanation: "En migræne" means "a migraine", a severe, throbbing pain, often on one side of the head. Light and noise often make it worse.

sentence.da: Når jeg har **migræne**, kan jeg ikke tåle lys.
sentence.en: When I have a migraine, I cannot stand light.

en mikrobølgeovn.explanation: "En mikrobølgeovn" means "a microwave oven", used to warm food fast. People often shorten it to en mikro (a microwave): Jeg varmer maden i mikroen (I warm the food in the microwave).

sentence.da: Man varmer mad op i en **mikrobølgeovn**.
sentence.en: You heat up food in a microwave oven.

en mikrofon.explanation: "En mikrofon" means "a microphone", a device that picks up your voice. On a call you may hear: Din mikrofon er slået fra (Your microphone is off). Slå din mikrofon til (Turn on your microphone).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke høre dig, fordi din **mikrofon** er slukket.
sentence.en: I cannot hear you because your microphone is off.

en mikroovn.explanation: "En mikroovn" means "a microwave", a shorter name for en mikrobølgeovn (a microwave oven).

sentence.da: Maden bliver varm hurtigt i en **mikroovn**.
sentence.en: The food gets hot fast in a microwave.

en mil.explanation: "En mil" means "a (Danish) mile", a measure of length equal to 10 km, far longer than an English mile. The plural is also mil: tre mil (three mil). It also lives on in the saying på mils afstand (from far away).

sentence.da: En **mil** er ti kilometer.
sentence.en: A mil is ten kilometers.

en milepæl.explanation: "En milepæl" means "a milestone". It is a marker by a road that shows how far you have come, and also an important step forward in a project or in life.

sentence.da: Vores første salg var en **milepæl** for firmaet.
sentence.en: Our first sale was a milestone for the company.

en milkshake.explanation: "En milkshake" means "a milkshake", a thick, sweet, cold drink.

sentence.da: En **milkshake** er lavet af mælk og is.
sentence.en: A milkshake is made of milk and ice cream.

en milliard.explanation: "En milliard" means "a billion" (a thousand million). Careful with the Danish word en billion: it means a trillion (a million million), not a billion.

sentence.da: Kina har over en **milliard** mennesker.
sentence.en: China has over a billion people.

en mindehøjtidelighed.explanation: "En mindehøjtidelighed" means "a memorial service", a solemn ceremony to remember people who have died, often held on a set date. It is built from minde (memory) and højtidelighed (ceremony).

sentence.da: Efter krigen holdt byen en **mindehøjtidelighed** for de faldne.
sentence.en: After the war the town held a memorial service for the fallen.

en mine.explanation: "En mine" means "a mine", a place where coal or metal is dug out of the ground, or a bomb hidden in the ground. It is also a look on the face, such as a sour or happy one. Do not mix it up with mine (my), as in mine børn (my children).

sentence.da: Hun lavede en sur **mine**, da hun smagte på suppen.
sentence.en: She made a sour face when she tasted the soup.

en minister.explanation: "En minister" means "a minister", a member of the government who leads one area. Put the area first to name the job: sundhedsminister (health minister).

sentence.da: Den nye **minister** vil bygge flere skoler.
sentence.en: The new minister wants to build more schools.

en minoritet.explanation: "En minoritet" means "a minority", a smaller part of a group or a country, for example people with their own language or religion.

sentence.da: Der bor en tysk **minoritet** i Sønderjylland.
sentence.en: A German minority lives in South Jutland.

en misforståelse.explanation: "En misforståelse" means "a misunderstanding", when two people understood something differently. The start mis- adds the idea of something going wrong or badly, as in mistillid (distrust) and mislykkes (to fail).

sentence.da: Undskyld, det var bare en **misforståelse**.
sentence.en: Sorry, it was just a misunderstanding.

en mission.explanation: "En mission" means "a mission", an important task that someone is sent to carry out, for example by an army or a company. It can also be a goal someone feels they must reach: Hendes mission er at redde havet (Her mission is to save the ocean).

sentence.da: Soldaterne fik en **mission** langt bag fjendens linjer.
sentence.en: The soldiers got a mission far behind enemy lines.

en mistanke.explanation: "En mistanke" means "a suspicion", a feeling that someone has done something wrong, without proof. It goes with om (about): at have mistanke om noget (to have a suspicion about something).

sentence.da: Politiet har en **mistanke**, men endnu ikke noget bevis.
sentence.en: The police have a suspicion, but no evidence yet.

en mobil.explanation: "En mobil" means "a mobile phone", the short everyday word for en mobiltelefon (a mobile phone). En telefon (a phone) can also be a landline.

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til dig fra min **mobil**.
sentence.en: I call you from my mobile phone.

en mobiltelefon.explanation: "En mobiltelefon" means "a mobile phone", the full word, made from mobil (mobile) and telefon (phone). In daily speech, people usually say en mobil (a mobile phone) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til min mor på min **mobiltelefon**.
sentence.en: I call my mother on my mobile phone.

en model.explanation: "En model" means "a model": a miniature of something, a type of car or a person who shows clothes. Hvilken model er bilen? (Which model is the car?)

sentence.da: Min onkel bygger en **model** af et skib.
sentence.en: My uncle is building a model of a ship.

en modspiller.explanation: "En modspiller" means "an opponent (in a game)", the person you play against, for example in chess or tennis. It is only for games and sports. For an opponent in a fight or an argument, use en modstander.

sentence.da: Man kan ikke spille skak uden en **modspiller**.
sentence.en: You cannot play chess without an opponent.

en modstand.explanation: "En modstand" means "a resistance", a pushing back against a plan, a change or an attacker. In physics it is also the force that slows a movement, as in luftmodstand (air resistance).

sentence.da: Planen mødte stor **modstand** blandt naboerne.
sentence.en: The plan met great resistance among the neighbors.

en modstander.explanation: "En modstander" means "an opponent", someone on the other side of a fight, an election, a match or an argument. It is wider than en modspiller, which is only for games.

sentence.da: Han er en stærk **modstander** af den nye lov.
sentence.en: He is a strong opponent of the new law.

en modsætning.explanation: "En modsætning" means "an opposite / a contrast", the way two things are completely different. The phrase i modsætning til (unlike) compares them: Jeg bliver hjemme, i modsætning til dig (I am staying home, unlike you).

sentence.da: Der er en stor **modsætning** mellem rig og fattig.
sentence.en: There is a big contrast between rich and poor.

en modtagelse.explanation: "En modtagelse" means "a reception". It is the act of getting something that arrives or of welcoming someone, and also how well a phone picks up a signal. At a hotel, the front desk is usually en reception.

sentence.da: Gæsterne fik en varm **modtagelse** af værten.
sentence.en: The guests got a warm reception from the host.

en modvilje.explanation: "En modvilje" means "a reluctance", a feeling of not wanting to do something. It is built from mod (against) and vilje (will). It is most often used as med modvilje (reluctantly).

sentence.da: Hun fortalte med **modvilje**, at hun måtte flytte.
sentence.en: She said with reluctance that she had to move.

en mole.explanation: "En mole" means "a pier", a long stone wall built out into the water to shelter a harbor from waves. People often walk out along it to look at the sea.

sentence.da: Der står et fyrtårn for enden af en **mole**.
sentence.en: There is a lighthouse at the end of a pier.

en moppe.explanation: "En moppe" means "a mop", a stick with soft strings or a flat pad at the end that you use with water.

sentence.da: Jeg vasker gulvet med en **moppe**.
sentence.en: I wash the floor with a mop.

en mor.explanation: "En mor" means "a mother". To talk about your own mother, say min mor (my mother). You can also use mor like a name when speaking to her: Hej, mor! (Hi, mom!).

sentence.da: Min **mor** er gift med min far.
sentence.en: My mother is married to my father.

en moral.explanation: "En moral" means "a moral / morale". It is the shared sense of right and wrong, and also the mood of a team or a workplace: Moralen på holdet er høj (Team morale is high).

sentence.da: Hans **moral** siger, at man aldrig må stjæle.
sentence.en: His morals say that you must never steal.

en morbror.explanation: "En morbror" means "an uncle", your mother's brother. Your father's brother is en farbror (an uncle).

sentence.da: Min **morbror** er min mors bror og bor i Roskilde.
sentence.en: My uncle is my mother's brother and lives in Roskilde.

en morder.explanation: "En morder" means "a murderer", a person who kills someone on purpose. It is built from mord (a murder), which also appears in en mordsag (a murder case).

sentence.da: Politiet leder efter en **morder**, der er flygtet.
sentence.en: The police are looking for a murderer who has escaped.

en morfar.explanation: "En morfar" means "a grandfather", your mother's father: mor (mother) plus far (father). Your father's father is en farfar (a grandfather, father's father).

sentence.da: Min **morfar** er min mors far.
sentence.en: My grandfather is my mother's father.

en morgen.explanation: "En morgen" means "a morning". Do not mix it up with i morgen (tomorrow) or i morges (this morning). Om morgenen means "in the morning" and "godmorgen" means "good morning".

sentence.da: Hver **morgen** spiser jeg morgenmad og drikker kaffe.
sentence.en: Every morning I eat breakfast and drink coffee.

en morgenkaffe.explanation: "En morgenkaffe" means "a morning coffee", the first cup of the day. It is built from morgen (morning) and kaffe (coffee). Morgen alone can also mean tomorrow, as in i morgen (tomorrow).

sentence.da: Min **morgenkaffe** kommer før morgenmaden.
sentence.en: My morning coffee comes before breakfast.

en morgenkåbe.explanation: "En morgenkåbe" means "a robe", a loose robe you wear at home in the morning, for example while you have breakfast.

sentence.da: En **morgenkåbe** tager man på, før man klæder sig på.
sentence.en: You put on a robe before you get dressed.

en morgenmadsbuffet.explanation: "En morgenmadsbuffet" means "a breakfast buffet", a spread of many kinds of food where you help yourself and take as much as you want. It is common at hotels, where it is often included in the price of the room.

sentence.da: Ved en **morgenmadsbuffet** tager man selv, hvad man vil have.
sentence.en: At a breakfast buffet, you take whatever you want yourself.

en morgenrutine.explanation: "En morgenrutine" means "a morning routine", the things you do every morning in the same order. It is built from morgen (morning) and rutine (routine). Watch the little word i: i morgen means tomorrow, not this morning.

sentence.da: Min **morgenrutine** er kaffe, avis og en kort gåtur.
sentence.en: My morning routine is coffee, newspaper and a short walk.

en mormor.explanation: "En mormor" means "a grandmother", your mother's mother: mor (mother) plus mor (mother) again. Your father's mother is en farmor (a grandmother, father's mother).

sentence.da: Min **mormor** er min mors mor.
sentence.en: My grandmother is my mother's mother.

en mose.explanation: "En mose" means "a bog", wet, soft land with peat. Do not mix it up with mos (moss), the small green plant.

sentence.da: Man kan synke i en **mose**, fordi jorden er våd og blød.
sentence.en: You can sink in a bog because the ground is wet and soft.

en moské.explanation: "En moské" means "a mosque", a building where Muslims come together to pray. It often has a tall tower called en minaret (a minaret).

sentence.da: Om fredagen mødes mange muslimer i en **moské**.
sentence.en: On Fridays, many Muslims meet in a mosque.

en moster.explanation: "En moster" means "an aunt", your mother's sister. Your father's sister is en faster (an aunt).

sentence.da: Min **moster** er min mors søster og bor i Odense.
sentence.en: My aunt is my mother's sister and lives in Odense.

en motor.explanation: "En motor" means "an engine". Danish uses one word for both engine and motor: Plæneklipperen har en lille motor (The lawn mower has a small motor). Bilens motor er gået i stå (The car's engine has stalled).

sentence.da: Bådens **motor** larmer meget, når vi sejler.
sentence.en: The boat's engine is very loud when we sail.

en motorcykel.explanation: "En motorcykel" means "a motorcycle". It is built from motor (engine) and cykel (bicycle). You cykle (bike) on a bicycle, but you køre (drive, ride) a motorcycle.

sentence.da: Min bror kører til arbejde på en stor **motorcykel**.
sentence.en: My brother rides to work on a big motorcycle.

en motorcyklist.explanation: "En motorcyklist" means "a motorcyclist", a person who rides a motorbike.

sentence.da: En **motorcyklist** skal altid bruge hjelm.
sentence.en: A motorcyclist must always wear a helmet.

en motorvej.explanation: "En motorvej" means "a highway", a big road with several lanes. It is built from motor (engine) and vej (road). Vej also means way, as in Hvilken vej skal vi gå? (Which way should we go?)

sentence.da: Vi skal køre på **motorvej** i to timer.
sentence.en: We have to drive on the highway for two hours.

en muffin.explanation: "En muffin" means "a muffin", a small, sweet baked treat in a paper cup.

sentence.da: Man bager en **muffin** af mel, sukker og æg.
sentence.en: You bake a muffin from flour, sugar and eggs.

en muffinform.explanation: "En muffinform" means "a muffin tin", the pan with small cups for baking muffins.

sentence.da: Hun hælder dejen i en **muffinform**.
sentence.en: She pours the batter into a muffin tin.

en muldvarp.explanation: "En muldvarp" means "a mole", the small animal that makes tunnels in the soil and pushes up small heaps of earth. It is also a person who secretly works for the other side from inside a group: Han var en muldvarp i firmaet (He was a mole in the company).

sentence.da: En **muldvarp** bor under jorden og ser næsten ingenting.
sentence.en: A mole lives under the ground and sees almost nothing.

en mulepose.explanation: "En mulepose" means "a tote bag", a sturdy cloth bag with two handles for carrying groceries, made to be used again and again.

sentence.da: Jeg lægger varerne i min **mulepose**, så jeg slipper for plastik.
sentence.en: I put the groceries in my tote bag, so I avoid plastic.

en mulighed.explanation: "En mulighed" means "a possibility", and also "an opportunity" or "an option": Det er en god mulighed (That is a good opportunity). Jeg har to muligheder (I have two options).

sentence.da: Det er den eneste **mulighed**, vi har.
sentence.en: It is the only option we have.

en mund.explanation: "En mund" means "a mouth", the opening in your face that you eat and speak with. Hold munden! means "Shut up!" and is rude.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser og taler med min **mund**.
sentence.en: I eat and talk with my mouth.

en munk.explanation: "En munk" means "a monk", a man who has given up ordinary life to live by the rules of a religious community.

sentence.da: En **munk** bor i et kloster og beder hver dag.
sentence.en: A monk lives in a monastery and prays every day.

en mur.explanation: "En mur" means "a wall" outside, like around a garden or on a house. For a wall inside a room, use en væg (a wall).

sentence.da: Byen har en gammel **mur** af sten.
sentence.en: The town has an old wall of stone.

en murer.explanation: "En murer" means "a bricklayer", a skilled worker who builds walls of brick or stone. The word is built on en mur (a wall).

sentence.da: En **murer** lægger sten på sten, indtil væggen er færdig.
sentence.en: A bricklayer lays stone on stone until the wall is finished.

en mursten.explanation: "En mursten" means "a brick", a hard block used to build walls. It is mur (wall) plus sten (stone). Sten alone is a stone: Han kaster en sten (He throws a stone).

sentence.da: En **mursten** er rød og lavet af ler.
sentence.en: A brick is red and made of clay.

en mus.explanation: "En mus" means "a mouse". It also means the computer mouse, en computermus (a computer mouse). The plural looks the same: to mus means "two mice". Do not mix it up with en rotte (a rat).

sentence.da: En **mus** er lille og spiser ost.
sentence.en: A mouse is small and eats cheese.

en musiker.explanation: "En musiker" means "a musician", someone who plays an instrument. It comes from musik (music).

sentence.da: Min onkel er **musiker** og spiller i et band.
sentence.en: My uncle is a musician and plays in a band.

en musikfestival.explanation: "En musikfestival" means "a music festival", a big event with many bands, often outdoors in summer. It is built from musik (music) and festival. The same musik is in en musiker (a musician).

sentence.da: Hver sommer hører vi mange bands på en **musikfestival**.
sentence.en: Every summer we hear many bands at a music festival.

en muskel.explanation: "En muskel" means "a muscle", the body part that lets you move. It joins other words, like muskelsmerter (muscle pain).

sentence.da: Du bruger en **muskel**, når du løfter armen.
sentence.en: You use a muscle when you lift your arm.

en musling.explanation: "En musling" means "a mussel" or "a clam", a small sea animal with two hard shells.

sentence.da: Hun åbner en **musling** og finder en perle.
sentence.en: She opens a mussel and finds a pearl.

en muslingeskal.explanation: "En muslingeskal" means "a seashell", the hard two-part shell of a clam or mussel, often found on the shore. A spiral shell is en snegleskal (a snail shell) instead.

sentence.da: En **muslingeskal** beskytter dyret, der bor inde i den.
sentence.en: A seashell protects the animal that lives inside it.

en myg.explanation: "En myg" means "a mosquito", a small flying insect that bites people and is common near water in summer. A fly that lands on food is en flue (a fly).

sentence.da: En **myg** stak mig i armen i nat.
sentence.en: A mosquito bit me on the arm last night.

en myndighed.explanation: "En myndighed" means "an authority", an official body that makes or enforces rules for the state, such as the police or a city office. The plural myndighederne (the authorities) covers the whole system of public offices.

sentence.da: Skattevæsenet er en **myndighed**, som opkræver skat.
sentence.en: The tax office is an authority that collects tax.

en myre.explanation: "En myre" means "an ant", a tiny insect that lives in large groups and works together.

sentence.da: En **myre** er lille og bærer mad hjem.
sentence.en: An ant is small and carries food home.

en myretue.explanation: "En myretue" means "an anthill", a mound made of soil and small pieces of plants where a colony of ants lives. It is built from en myre (an ant) and en tue (a small mound).

sentence.da: Tusindvis af myrer bor i en **myretue**.
sentence.en: Thousands of ants live in an anthill.

en myte.explanation: "En myte" means "a myth", an old story about gods and heroes that people told to explain the world. It also means a common belief that is not true: Det er en myte, at man kun bruger ti procent af hjernen (It is a myth that people only use ten percent of the brain).

sentence.da: Fortællingen om Thor og hans hammer er en gammel **myte**.
sentence.en: The tale of Thor and his hammer is an old myth.

en måde.explanation: "En måde" means "a way" of doing something. På den måde means "in that way", and "på en eller anden måde" means "somehow". Do not mix it up with en vej (a road or path).

sentence.da: Det er en god **måde** at lære på.
sentence.en: That is a good way to learn.

en måge.explanation: "En måge" means "a seagull", a bird you see at the sea and in harbors.

sentence.da: En **måge** flyver over havet og leder efter fisk.
sentence.en: A seagull flies over the sea looking for fish.

en måler.explanation: "En måler" means "a meter / gauge", an instrument that shows how much of something there is or how much you have used, such as electricity or water at home.

sentence.da: En **måler** viser, hvor meget strøm vi bruger hjemme.
sentence.en: A meter shows how much electricity we use at home.

en målgruppe.explanation: "En målgruppe" means "a target group", the kind of people that a product, an ad or a program is made for, described by things like age or interests.

sentence.da: Børnebøger har børn og forældre som **målgruppe**.
sentence.en: Children's books have children and parents as the target group.

en måling.explanation: "En måling" means "a measurement", the act of finding the size or amount of something, and the number you get. In the news, en måling on its own often means an opinion poll. Do not mix it up with maling (paint), which is spelled with a plain a, not å.

sentence.da: En **måling** af rummet viste, at det er fire meter langt.
sentence.en: A measurement of the room showed that it is four meters long.

en målmand.explanation: "En målmand" means "a goalkeeper", the player who stops the ball from going into the goal. It is built from mål (goal) and mand (man). Mål also means an aim in life: Mit mål er at lære dansk (My goal is to learn Danish).

sentence.da: Han vil være **målmand**, fordi han griber bolden godt.
sentence.en: He wants to be a goalkeeper because he catches the ball well.

en måne.explanation: "En måne" means "a moon", the round object that shines in the night sky. Do not mix it up with en måned (a month), which starts the same.

sentence.da: En **måne** går rundt om en planet.
sentence.en: A moon goes around a planet.

en måned.explanation: "En måned" means "a month", one of the twelve parts of a year. Om måneden means "per month", i denne måned means "this month", and næste måned means "next month".

sentence.da: Der er cirka tredive dage i en **måned**.
sentence.en: There are about thirty days in a month.

en mår.explanation: "En mår" means "a marten", a slim, quick animal with soft fur that hunts small animals and climbs trees. Two kinds live in Denmark: skovmår (pine marten) in forests and husmår (stone marten) near houses.

sentence.da: En **mår** er et slankt rovdyr og klatrer godt.
sentence.en: A marten is a slim predator and climbs well.

en mælkebøtte.explanation: "En mælkebøtte" means "a dandelion", a common yellow wildflower in grass. Its stem has a white, milky juice, and mælk (milk) is the first part of the name.

sentence.da: En **mælkebøtte** er gul, men bliver senere hvid og luftig.
sentence.en: A dandelion is yellow, but later becomes white and fluffy.

en mængde.explanation: "En mængde" means "an amount", how much of something there is: en stor mængde vand (a large amount of water). For things you can count, use et antal (a number): et antal bøger (a number of books).

sentence.da: Du skal bruge en lille **mængde** salt.
sentence.en: You need a small amount of salt.

en møbelforretning.explanation: "En møbelforretning" means "a furniture store", a place that sells furniture for the home. Forretning also means a business deal: at gøre en god forretning (to make a good deal).

sentence.da: I en **møbelforretning** kan man købe sofaer og borde.
sentence.en: In a furniture store you can buy sofas and tables.

en mølle.explanation: "En mølle" means "a mill", a building or machine that turns wheat into flour. A windmill is en vindmølle.

sentence.da: Bageren køber mel fra den gamle **mølle**.
sentence.en: The baker buys flour from the old mill.

en mønt.explanation: "En mønt" means "a coin", used for small payments. Paper money is en seddel (a banknote).

sentence.da: En **mønt** er rund og lavet af metal.
sentence.en: A coin is round and made of metal.

et madbud.explanation: "Et madbud" means "a food delivery person", someone who brings meals from restaurants to customers. Bud alone means "messenger".

sentence.da: Et **madbud** kommer med maden hjem til døren.
sentence.en: A food delivery person brings the food home to the door.

et magasin.explanation: "Et magasin" means "a magazine", with articles and photos. In everyday speech, Danes often say et blad (a magazine) instead.

sentence.da: Jeg læser et **magasin** i venteværelset.
sentence.en: I read a magazine in the waiting room.

et maleri.explanation: "Et maleri" means "a painting", a finished picture made with paint. The person who makes it is en maler (a painter).

sentence.da: Der hænger et flot **maleri** over sofaen.
sentence.en: A beautiful painting hangs over the sofa.

et mandskab.explanation: "Et mandskab" means "a crew", the people who work together on a ship, a plane or a rescue operation. It is used for the group as a whole, not for one person.

sentence.da: Skibet har et **mandskab** på tyve personer.
sentence.en: The ship has a crew of twenty people.

et manuskript.explanation: "Et manuskript" means "a manuscript" and also "a script", the written text of a film, a play or a speech, before it is finished or performed.

sentence.da: Skuespillerne har lært deres **manuskript** udenad før premieren.
sentence.en: The actors have learned their script by heart before the premiere.

et maraton.explanation: "Et maraton" means "a marathon", a long race of about 42 kilometers. Danes also say et maratonløb (a marathon race) for the same thing.

sentence.da: Hun træner hårdt til sit første **maraton**.
sentence.en: She is training hard for her first marathon.

et mareridt.explanation: "Et mareridt" means "a nightmare", both a bad dream and a terrible situation: Trafikken var et mareridt (The traffic was a nightmare).

sentence.da: Jeg havde et forfærdeligt **mareridt** i nat.
sentence.en: I had a terrible nightmare last night.

et marked.explanation: "Et marked" means "a market", such as an open-air place where people sell fruit, vegetables or second-hand things.

sentence.da: Vi køber frugt og grøntsager på et **marked**.
sentence.en: We buy fruit and vegetables at a market.

et marsvin.explanation: "Et marsvin" means "a guinea pig", the small furry pet, and also "a porpoise", a small sea mammal. The situation shows which one is meant.

sentence.da: Vores **marsvin** elsker gulerødder og bor i et bur.
sentence.en: Our guinea pig loves carrots and lives in a cage.

et materiale.explanation: "Et materiale" means "a material", what something is made of. It can also mean information or study material: Jeg læser materialet (I read the material).

sentence.da: Stål er et stærkt **materiale**.
sentence.en: Steel is a strong material.

et medicinskab.explanation: "Et medicinskab" means "a medicine cabinet", a small cabinet where you keep medicine and bandages. It is built from medicin (medicine) and skab (cabinet).

sentence.da: Pillerne ligger i et lille **medicinskab** på badeværelset.
sentence.en: The pills are in a small medicine cabinet in the bathroom.

et medie.explanation: "Et medie" means "a medium", a way of sharing news or information, such as newspapers, TV or the internet. Danes mostly use the plural: medierne (the media) report on events.

sentence.da: Radioen er et **medie**, som formidler nyheder og musik.
sentence.en: The radio is a medium that spreads news and music.

et medlem.explanation: "Et medlem" means "a member" of a group, club or team: Hun er medlem af en klub (She is a member of a club). Add af (of) to say which group.

sentence.da: Min bror er **medlem** af en fodboldklub.
sentence.en: My brother is a member of a soccer club.

et medlemskab.explanation: "Et medlemskab" means "a membership", being a member of a club, a gym or a group. The ending -skab turns a word into a state or a relationship, as in et venskab (a friendship).

sentence.da: Et **medlemskab** i klubben koster hundrede kroner om måneden.
sentence.en: A membership in the club costs a hundred kroner a month.

et mellemnavn.explanation: "Et mellemnavn" means "a middle name", a name between the first and last name. It is made of mellem (between) and et navn (a name), and mellem also appears in et mellemmåltid (a snack between meals).

sentence.da: Marie er mit **mellemnavn**.
sentence.en: Marie is my middle name.

et menneske.explanation: "Et menneske" means "a human being", as opposed to an animal. Its plural mennesker is the everyday word for "people", as in mange mennesker (many people).

sentence.da: Du er et **menneske**, ikke et dyr.
sentence.en: You are a human being, not an animal.

et menukort.explanation: "Et menukort" means "a menu", the list of dishes and drinks in a restaurant. You can ask a waiter Må jeg se menukortet? (May I see the menu?). En menu is a set meal with several courses.

sentence.da: Vi ser på et **menukort** i restauranten.
sentence.en: We look at a menu in the restaurant.

et mesterskab.explanation: "Et mesterskab" means "a championship", a competition to find the best. Short forms are DM (Danish championship), EM (European) and VM (World). The ending -skab is the same as in et medlemskab (a membership).

sentence.da: Vinderen af et **mesterskab** får en guldmedalje.
sentence.en: The winner of a championship gets a gold medal.

et metal.explanation: "Et metal" means "a metal", such as gold. It is also the name of a loud music style: Jeg hører metal (I listen to metal).

sentence.da: Aluminium er et let **metal**.
sentence.en: Aluminum is a light metal.

et middagsselskab.explanation: "Et middagsselskab" means "a dinner party", an evening where people are invited to eat a meal together, often at home. Selskab alone means "company", for guests or for a business: et forsikringsselskab (an insurance company).

sentence.da: Vi har inviteret venner til et **middagsselskab** på lørdag.
sentence.en: We have invited friends to a dinner party on Saturday.

et middel.explanation: "Et middel" means "a means", a way of reaching a goal, and also "a remedy", a product that helps against something: et middel mod (a remedy for). The plural midler also means "funds", as in offentlige midler (public funds).

sentence.da: Motion er et godt **middel** mod stress.
sentence.en: Exercise is a good remedy for stress.

et militær.explanation: "Et militær" means "a military", a country's armed forces. Militær also describes things: et militært køretøj (a military vehicle).

sentence.da: Landets **militær** har både soldater og skibe.
sentence.en: The country's military has both soldiers and ships.

et miljø.explanation: "Et miljø" means "an environment", the air, water and land around us, and also the surroundings people live or work in: et godt arbejdsmiljø (a good work environment).

sentence.da: Plastik i havet er dårligt for vores **miljø**.
sentence.en: Plastic in the sea is bad for our environment.

et mindretal.explanation: "Et mindretal" means "a minority", the smaller part of a group, fewer than half of the people or of the seats. It is used in politics and for any group that is outnumbered.

sentence.da: Kun et **mindretal** stemte for forslaget, så det faldt.
sentence.en: Only a minority voted for the proposal, so it failed.

et ministerium.explanation: "Et ministerium" means "a ministry", a part of the government headed by a minister. In names it is joined to the topic: Finansministeriet (the Ministry of Finance).

sentence.da: Skatteministeriet er et **ministerium**, der styrer skatten i landet.
sentence.en: The Ministry of Taxation is a ministry that manages taxes in the country.

et minut.explanation: "Et minut" means "a minute". To ask someone to wait, you can say Vent et øjeblik (wait a moment) or Vent et minut (wait a minute).

sentence.da: Et **minut** er tres sekunder.
sentence.en: A minute is sixty seconds.

et mirakel.explanation: "Et mirakel" means "a miracle", an event so unlikely that it seems impossible, and in religion an act of God that breaks the laws of nature.

sentence.da: Det er et **mirakel**, at han overlevede ulykken uden skader.
sentence.en: It is a miracle that he survived the accident without injuries.

et missil.explanation: "Et missil" means "a missile", a weapon that flies and explodes. A rocket for space or fireworks is en raket (a rocket).

sentence.da: Et **missil** ramte en bygning i nat.
sentence.en: A missile hit a building last night.

et modermærke.explanation: "Et modermærke" means "a mole", a small dark spot on the skin that you are born with or get over time. It is not the animal, which is en muldvarp.

sentence.da: Lægen kigger på det mørke **modermærke** på min ryg.
sentence.en: The doctor looks at the dark mole on my back.

et modersmål.explanation: "Et modersmål" means "a mother tongue", the speech you learned first as a child. Mål is an old word for speech.

sentence.da: Mit **modersmål** er engelsk, men jeg lærer dansk.
sentence.en: My mother tongue is English, but I am learning Danish.

et modeshow.explanation: "Et modeshow" means "a fashion show", an event where models walk and show new clothes. Mode (fashion) is joined to the English word show.

sentence.da: Til et **modeshow** går modeller rundt i nyt tøj.
sentence.en: At a fashion show, models walk around in new clothes.

et modsætningsord.explanation: "Et modsætningsord" means "an antonym", a word that has the reverse meaning of another word.

sentence.da: Varm er et **modsætningsord** til kold.
sentence.en: Warm is an antonym of cold.

et molekyle.explanation: "Et molekyle" means "a molecule", a very small group of atoms joined together, such as in sugar or in air.

sentence.da: Hvert **molekyle** i vand har to brintatomer og ét iltatom.
sentence.en: Each molecule in water has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

et monster.explanation: "Et monster" means "a monster". Do not mix it up with et mønster (a pattern), which looks almost the same.

sentence.da: Barnet er bange for et **monster** under sengen.
sentence.en: The child is afraid of a monster under the bed.

et monument.explanation: "Et monument" means "a monument", a big structure that honors a person or an event. Use for to say who it honors: et monument for kongen (a monument for the king).

sentence.da: Det store **monument** minder om krigen.
sentence.en: The big monument is a reminder of the war.

et mord.explanation: "Et mord" means "a murder", when one person kills another on purpose. You often hear it in crime news and stories: Han blev anholdt for mordet (He was arrested for the murder).

sentence.da: Politiet undersøger det **mord**, der skete i går.
sentence.en: The police are investigating the murder that happened yesterday.

et motel.explanation: "Et motel" means "a motel", a simple hotel by the road for people traveling by car.

sentence.da: Vi sover på et **motel** ved motorvejen.
sentence.en: We are sleeping at a motel by the highway.

et motiv.explanation: "Et motiv" means "a motive", the reason behind someone's action, and also "a subject", what a photo or a painting shows: Motivet er en kirke (The subject is a church).

sentence.da: Politiet leder stadig efter et **motiv** for forbrydelsen.
sentence.en: The police are still looking for a motive for the crime.

et museum.explanation: "Et museum" means "a museum", a place with art, history or science to look at. You say på museet for "at the museum".

sentence.da: Vi ser gamle ting på et **museum**.
sentence.en: We see old things at a museum.

et mysterium.explanation: "Et mysterium" means "a mystery", something strange or hidden that nobody can explain.

sentence.da: Hvordan pyramiderne blev bygget, er stadig et **mysterium**.
sentence.en: How the pyramids were built is still a mystery.

et mål.explanation: "Et mål" means "a goal", in life and in sports: Mit mål er at løbe et maraton (My goal is to run a marathon). Han scorede to mål (He scored two goals).

sentence.da: Mit **mål** er at tale godt dansk.
sentence.en: My goal is to speak good Danish.

et målebånd.explanation: "Et målebånd" means "a tape measure", a long, flexible strip with numbers that you use to measure length. It is built from at måle (to measure) and et bånd (a band).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **målebånd**, når jeg køber møbler.
sentence.en: I use a tape measure when I buy furniture.

et målebæger.explanation: "Et målebæger" means "a measuring cup", a cup with marks that show how much liquid or flour you pour. It is built from at måle (to measure) and et bæger (a cup).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **målebæger** til at måle sukker.
sentence.en: I use a measuring cup to measure sugar.

et måltid.explanation: "Et måltid" means "a meal", any occasion when you sit down to eat, like breakfast, lunch or dinner. It is the occasion, not the food itself: for "food" Danes say mad.

sentence.da: Dagens vigtigste **måltid** er morgenmad.
sentence.en: The most important meal of the day is breakfast.

et månedskort.explanation: "Et månedskort" means "a monthly pass", a ticket you can use as much as you like for a month. It is built from måned (month) and kort (card).

sentence.da: Med et **månedskort** kan jeg tage bussen hver dag.
sentence.en: With a monthly pass, I can take the bus every day.

et mærke.explanation: "Et mærke" means "a brand", and also "a mark" on a surface: et mærke på væggen (a mark on the wall).

sentence.da: Det er et dyrt **mærke**, men jakken er flot.
sentence.en: It is an expensive brand, but the jacket is nice.

et møbel.explanation: "Et møbel" means "a piece of furniture", such as a chair, a table or a bed. The plural møbler means "furniture" in general: Vi køber nye møbler (We are buying new furniture).

sentence.da: En sofa er et **møbel**.
sentence.en: A sofa is a piece of furniture.

et møde.explanation: "Et møde" means "a meeting", for example at work.

sentence.da: Min chef har et **møde** i dag.
sentence.en: My boss has a meeting today.

et mødelokale.explanation: "Et mødelokale" means "a meeting room", a room at a workplace used for meetings. Lokale is a room in a public or work building, while et værelse is a room in a home or a hotel.

sentence.da: Kollegerne sidder i et **mødelokale** og planlægger det nye projekt.
sentence.en: The colleagues are sitting in a meeting room and planning the new project.

et mønster.explanation: "Et mønster" means "a pattern", on cloth or in how things repeat.

sentence.da: Der er et fint **mønster** på kjolen.
sentence.en: There is a nice pattern on the dress.

mad.explanation: "Mad" means "food" in general: Jeg elsker dansk mad (I love Danish food). For one dish, use en ret (a dish). En mad means "a sandwich", so do not mix them up.

sentence.da: Jeg er sulten og vil have **mad**.
sentence.en: I am hungry and want food.

madlavning.explanation: "Madlavning" means "cooking", the activity of making meals. To say someone is cooking right now, use Han laver mad (He is cooking).

sentence.da: Ved **madlavning** bruger vi en gryde og en pande.
sentence.en: When cooking, we use a pot and a pan.

madpapir.explanation: "Et madpapir" means "sandwich paper", the thin paper you wrap sandwiches in to take with you. It keeps the bread from drying out.

sentence.da: Jeg pakker madderne ind i **madpapir** og lægger dem i tasken.
sentence.en: I wrap the sandwiches in sandwich paper and put them in the bag.

madspild.explanation: "Et madspild" means "food waste", food that is bought or made but never eaten. It is built from mad (food) and spild (waste).

sentence.da: **Madspild** sker, når vi køber mere mad, end vi spiser.
sentence.en: Food waste happens when we buy more food than we eat.

mager.explanation: "Mager" means "lean" for food and "skinny" for people: Kyllingebryst er magert (Chicken breast is lean). For a person, it can sound negative, so tynd (thin) is milder.

sentence.da: En **mager** bøf har meget lidt fedt.
sentence.en: A lean steak has very little fat.

magi.explanation: "En magi" means "magic", the power to make impossible things happen, as in stories with spells. It also means a special, hard-to-explain charm: Der er magi i luften (There is magic in the air).

sentence.da: I eventyret bruger heksen **magi** til at forvandle prinsen til en frø.
sentence.en: In the fairy tale the witch uses magic to turn the prince into a frog.

magisk.explanation: "Magisk" means "magical", like magic in stories: en magisk bog (a magical book). It also describes a wonderful moment: Det var magisk! (It was magical!)

sentence.da: Troldmanden har en **magisk** stav i hånden.
sentence.en: The wizard has a magic wand in his hand.

magtfuld.explanation: "Magtfuld" means "powerful", for someone who has power over others, like rulers and big companies: en magtfuld direktør (a powerful director). For body strength, use stærk (strong).

sentence.da: Kongen var meget **magtfuld** og styrede hele landet.
sentence.en: The king was very powerful and ruled the whole country.

maj.explanation: "Maj" means "May" and sounds like the English word "my". Month names start with a small letter in Danish, so you write maj in the middle of a sentence: Det er varmt i maj (It is warm in May).

sentence.da: **Maj** kommer efter april og før juni.
sentence.en: May comes after April and before June.

majs.explanation: "Majs" means "corn", the yellow kind you eat as a vegetable. It is used without en: Jeg spiser majs (I eat corn).

sentence.da: Popcorn er lavet af **majs**.
sentence.en: Popcorn is made of corn.

makeup.explanation: "Makeup" means "makeup", the same word as in English. To put it on, say tage makeup på: Hun tager makeup på (She puts on makeup).

sentence.da: Hun bruger **makeup** på øjne og læber.
sentence.en: She uses makeup on her eyes and lips.

maksimal.explanation: "Maksimal" means "maximum", the biggest amount that is allowed or possible: et maksimalt antal pladser (a maximum number of seats).

sentence.da: Bilen kører med **maksimal** hastighed på motorvejen.
sentence.en: The car drives at maximum speed on the highway.

malerisk.explanation: "Malerisk" means "picturesque", so lovely to look at that it seems made for a picture. It is used for places such as villages, views and old streets.

sentence.da: Den lille by med gamle huse og smalle gader er **malerisk**.
sentence.en: The small town with old houses and narrow streets is picturesque.

maling.explanation: "Maling" means "paint". A picture on a wall is et maleri (a painting), not maling.

sentence.da: Vi skal bruge blå **maling** til soveværelset.
sentence.en: We need blue paint for the bedroom.

man.explanation: "Man" means "you" or "one" for anybody, people in general. Compare Du kan købe billetter (You can buy tickets — said to one person) with Man kan købe billetter her (You can buy tickets here — anyone can). Do not mix it up with en mand (a man).

sentence.da: Her må **man** ikke parkere.
sentence.en: You may not park here.

man skal ikke skue hunden på hårene.explanation: "Man skal ikke skue hunden på hårene" means "don't judge a book by its cover". Literally it says you should not judge the dog by its hair. Skue is an old word for look at, and the saying is used when someone turns out different from how they looked.

forms.da: Man skal ikke skue hunden på hårene!
forms.en: Don't judge a book by its cover!

forms.da: Jeg troede, han var sur, men man skal ikke skue hunden på hårene
forms.en: I thought he was grumpy, but don't judge a book by its cover

related.da: det er ikke guld alt, hvad der glimrer
related.en: all that glitters is not gold

sentence.da: Hun ser streng ud, men **man skal ikke skue hunden på hårene**.
sentence.en: She looks strict, but don't judge a book by its cover.

mandag.explanation: "En mandag" means "a Monday". På mandag means "on Monday" (the coming one), om mandagen means "on Mondays" in general, and "i mandags" means "last Monday". Day names start with a small letter in Danish.

sentence.da: Ugen begynder med **mandag**.
sentence.en: The week begins with Monday.

mandlig.explanation: "Mandlig" means "male" and is built on mand (man). It is used for people and animals: en mandlig kollega (a male colleague), en mandlig løve (a male lion).

sentence.da: Han er en **mandlig** sygeplejerske.
sentence.en: He is a male nurse.
