manerer.explanation: "Manerer" means "manners", the way a person behaves around others. It is always plural in this meaning: Han har gode manerer (He has good manners).

sentence.da: Børn lærer **manerer**, når de spiser sammen med de voksne.
sentence.en: Children learn manners when they eat together with the adults.

mange.explanation: "Mange" means "many" for things you can count: mange biler (many cars). For things you cannot count, like water, use meget (a lot, much): meget vand (a lot of water).

sentence.da: Jeg har **mange** venner.
sentence.en: I have many friends.

mange tak.explanation: "Mange tak" means "many thanks", a bit stronger than plain tak (thanks). Add for and what you are thankful for: Mange tak for hjælpen (Thank you very much for the help). The reply is selv tak (you're welcome) or ingen årsag (no problem).

forms.en: Thank you very much for the help.

sentence.da: Her er din kaffe. – **Mange tak**!
sentence.en: Here is your coffee. – Thank you very much!

mangelfuld.explanation: "Mangelfuld" means "deficient" or "inadequate", for something that lacks parts or is not good enough, such as information, work or equipment. It is built from mangel (shortage) and -fuld (full of), so it describes something with parts missing.

sentence.da: Forklaringen var **mangelfuld**, og vi forstod den ikke.
sentence.en: The explanation was inadequate and we did not understand it.

mangfoldighed.explanation: "En mangfoldighed" means "diversity", many different kinds existing side by side, in people, cultures or nature: en mangfoldighed af farver (a variety of colors).

sentence.da: Naturen byder på en stor **mangfoldighed** af planter og dyr.
sentence.en: Nature offers a great diversity of plants and animals.

manglende.explanation: "Manglende" means "missing", for something that is not there but should be: manglende betaling (missing payment). It stays the same for en-words, et-words and plurals.

sentence.da: Den **manglende** brik til puslespillet lå under sofaen.
sentence.en: The missing piece of the puzzle was under the sofa.

marcipan.explanation: "Marcipan" means "marzipan", a sweet paste of almonds and sugar: Kransekagen er lavet af marcipan (The ring cake is made of marzipan).

sentence.da: Kagen er fyldt med **marcipan** og mandler.
sentence.en: The cake is filled with marzipan and almonds.

marihuana.explanation: "En marihuana" means "marijuana", the dried parts of the hemp plant that people use to get high. Danish spells it with an h where English has a j.

sentence.da: Det er ulovligt at sælge **marihuana** i Danmark.
sentence.en: It is illegal to sell marijuana in Denmark.

markant.explanation: "Markant" means "marked" or "distinctive", clearly noticeable because it stands out. It is used for a change or a difference, and also for a person or feature with a strong presence: en markant politiker (a prominent politician).

sentence.da: Der er en **markant** forskel mellem sommer og vinter her.
sentence.en: There is a marked difference between summer and winter here.

marmelade.explanation: "Marmelade" means "jam" or "marmalade", a sweet fruit spread for bread: Jeg smører marmelade på brødet (I spread jam on the bread).

sentence.da: Hun spiser brød med smør og **marmelade**.
sentence.en: She eats bread with butter and jam.

marmor.explanation: "Et marmor" means "marble", a hard, smooth rock used for floors, kitchen counters and art: et gulv af marmor (a floor of marble).

sentence.da: Statuen er hugget i **marmor**, ikke i træ.
sentence.en: The statue is carved in marble, not in wood.

marts.explanation: "Marts" means "March". Month names start with a small letter in Danish. Dates are said like den tiende marts (the tenth of March).

sentence.da: Efter februar kommer **marts**.
sentence.en: After February comes March.

masser af.explanation: "Masser af" means "lots of". It is informal, and it works for things you can count and things you cannot: masser af mad (lots of food), masser af venner (lots of friends).

sentence.da: Vi har **masser af** tid i dag.
sentence.en: We have lots of time today.

matematik.explanation: "Matematik" means "math". The short form is matte.

sentence.da: I **matematik** lærer vi at regne med tal.
sentence.en: In math we learn to calculate with numbers.

materiel.explanation: "Materiel" means "material", about things you can touch or own, as opposed to ideas and feelings: materielle goder (material goods). Do not mix it up with et materiale, which is a substance such as wood or cloth.

sentence.da: Branden gav kun **materiel** skade, og ingen blev såret.
sentence.en: The fire caused only material damage, and nobody was hurt.

mayonnaise.explanation: "Mayonnaise" means "mayonnaise", the thick white sauce. In everyday talk, Danes often shorten it to mayo.

sentence.da: Man laver **mayonnaise** af æg og olie.
sentence.en: You make mayonnaise from egg and oil.

med.explanation: "Med" means "with". Its opposite is uden (without): kaffe uden mælk (coffee without milk). It is also used for coming or going along: tage med (to take along), gå med (to go along).

forms.en: a cup of coffee with milk

sentence.da: Jeg drikker kaffe **med** mælk.
sentence.en: I drink coffee with milk.

med andre ord.explanation: "Med andre ord" means "in other words" and says the same thing again or sums it up: Bilen er gået i stykker. Med andre ord må vi tage toget (The car broke down. In other words, we must take the train).

sentence.da: Han er syg. **Med andre ord** kommer han ikke.
sentence.en: He is sick. In other words, he is not coming.

med det samme.explanation: "Med det samme" means "right away" or "immediately". For something soon but not this second, use om lidt (in a little while).

sentence.da: Jeg kommer **med det samme**.
sentence.en: I'm coming right away.

med forsæt.explanation: "Med forsæt" means "on purpose", done deliberately, with a plan to do it. Everyday talk uses med vilje (deliberately), while med forsæt is what courts and news say when a harmful act was meant: Branden blev påsat med forsæt (The fire was set on purpose).

sentence.da: Retten mener, at han ødelagde bilen **med forsæt**.
sentence.en: The court believes he destroyed the car on purpose.

med hensyn til.explanation: "Med hensyn til" means "regarding", used to name the topic you are about to talk about: Med hensyn til maden har vi et problem (Regarding the food, we have a problem).

sentence.da: **Med hensyn til** mødet i morgen kan jeg desværre ikke komme.
sentence.en: Regarding the meeting tomorrow, I unfortunately cannot come.

medfølelse.explanation: "En medfølelse" means "compassion", the feeling of sharing someone's pain and wanting to help. It is built from med (with) and følelse (feeling), so it is feeling with someone, not looking down on them.

sentence.da: Hun viste **medfølelse** og holdt ham i hånden, da han græd.
sentence.en: She showed compassion and held his hand when he cried.

medicin.explanation: "En medicin" means "a medicine", something you take when you are ill.

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og tager **medicin**.
sentence.en: I am sick and take medicine.

medicinsk.explanation: "Medicinsk" means "medical", about illness and how it is cured: en medicinsk undersøgelse (a medical exam). It also describes treatment with medicine: medicinsk behandling (treatment with medicine).

sentence.da: Lægen mener, at smerten har en **medicinsk** årsag.
sentence.en: The doctor thinks the pain has a medical cause.

medlidenhed.explanation: "En medlidenhed" means "pity", the sad feeling for someone who suffers. It can feel like looking down on a person, so some do not want it: Jeg vil ikke have din medlidenhed (I do not want your pity).

sentence.da: Han følte **medlidenhed** med hunden, som stod alene i regnen.
sentence.en: He felt pity for the dog that stood alone in the rain.

medmindre.explanation: "Medmindre" means "unless", introducing the only case where the main statement is not true: Jeg kommer, medmindre jeg bliver syg (I will come unless I get sick).

sentence.da: Vi tager til stranden, **medmindre** det regner.
sentence.en: We are going to the beach unless it rains.

megen.explanation: "Megen" means "much" and is used with en-words you cannot count: megen tid (much time). It is mostly used in sentences with ikke (not) or with for (too): for megen støj (too much noise).

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke **megen** tid.
sentence.en: I do not have much time.

meget.explanation: "Meget" means "very" before a describing word: meget god (very good). With amounts it means "a lot" or "much": meget vand (a lot of water). For things you can count, use mange (many) instead.

forms.en: I have a lot of time.

sentence.da: Det er **meget** koldt i dag.
sentence.en: It is very cold today.

mel.explanation: "Mel" means "flour", the white powder you bake with. Do not mix it up with mælk (milk), which looks similar.

sentence.da: Jeg bager brød med **mel**.
sentence.en: I bake bread with flour.

mellem.explanation: "Mellem" means "between", for places, times and amounts: mellem to og tre (between two and three). It also works for a difference: forskellen mellem dem (the difference between them).

forms.en: between the house and the forest

sentence.da: Banken ligger **mellem** posthuset og skolen.
sentence.en: The bank is between the post office and the school.

mellemøsten.explanation: "Mellemøsten" means "the Middle East". It is built from mellem (between) and øst (east). Mellem also works alone: Jeg sidder mellem Anna og Tom (I sit between Anna and Tom).

forms.en: to travel to the Middle East
the war in the Middle East

sentence.da: Det er varmt og tørt i **Mellemøsten**.
sentence.en: It is hot and dry in the Middle East.

men.explanation: "Men" means "but". It joins two ideas that go against each other: Jeg er træt, men jeg kommer (I am tired, but I am coming). Do not mix it up with mens (while).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt, **men** glad.
sentence.en: I am tired, but happy.

meningsfuld.explanation: "Meningsfuld" means "meaningful", for something that has a point or feels worth your time: et meningsfuldt job (a meaningful job).

sentence.da: Samtalen var **meningsfuld**, fordi vi endelig forstod hinanden.
sentence.en: The conversation was meaningful because we finally understood each other.

meningsløs.explanation: "Meningsløs" means "meaningless", with no point or sense: en meningsløs krig (a senseless war). The ending -løs means "without", as in hjælpeløs (helpless).

sentence.da: Diskussionen var **meningsløs**, fordi ingen ville lytte.
sentence.en: The discussion was pointless because nobody wanted to listen.

menneskehed.explanation: "En menneskehed" means "humanity", all people taken together. The quality of being kind and humane is a different word: menneskelighed (humaneness).

sentence.da: Mange drømmer om en **menneskehed** uden krig.
sentence.en: Many dream of a humanity without war.

menneskelig.explanation: "Menneskelig" means "human", about people. It can also mean kind and understanding: en menneskelig chef (a kind boss).

sentence.da: Det er en **menneskelig** fejl, ikke en computerfejl.
sentence.en: It is a human mistake, not a computer error.

menneskerettigheder.explanation: "Menneskerettigheder" means "human rights", the basic rights that every person has, whoever they are and wherever they live, such as the right to live and speak freely.

sentence.da: **Menneskerettigheder** gælder for alle, uanset hvor man bor.
sentence.en: Human rights apply to everyone, no matter where one lives.

mens.explanation: "Mens" means "while". It joins two things that happen at the same time: Hun synger, mens hun laver mad (She sings while she cooks). Do not mix it up with men (but).

sentence.da: Jeg læser, **mens** du sover.
sentence.en: I read while you sleep.

mental sundhed.explanation: "En mental sundhed" means "mental health", how well your mind and feelings are doing, not only whether you are ill: at passe på sin mentale sundhed (to look after your mental health).

sentence.da: God **mental sundhed** handler om søvn, venner og ro i hverdagen.
sentence.en: Good mental health is about sleep, friends and calm in everyday life.

mentalt.explanation: "Mentalt" means "mentally", in the mind rather than the body: Jeg er mentalt træt (I am mentally tired).

sentence.da: Før løbet forbereder løberne sig både fysisk og **mentalt**.
sentence.en: Before the race the runners prepare both physically and mentally.

mere.explanation: "Mere" means "more" for amounts you cannot count: mere vand (more water). Before a describing word it makes a comparison: mere interessant (more interesting). Ikke mere means "no longer": Jeg bor ikke her mere (I don't live here anymore). For things you can count, use flere: flere biler (more cars).

sentence.da: Jeg er sulten og vil have **mere** mad.
sentence.en: I am hungry and want more food.

mest.explanation: "Mest" means "most" or "mostly". Before a describing word it means "the most": mest interessant (most interesting). With kan lide (like) it means "like best": Jeg kan mest lide kaffe (I like coffee best).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **mest** lide kaffe.
sentence.en: I like coffee the most.

mexicansk.explanation: "Mexicansk" means "Mexican" and describes things from Mexico. A person from Mexico is en mexicaner (a Mexican).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **mexicansk** mad hver fredag.
sentence.en: We eat Mexican food every Friday.

middelalderen.explanation: "Middelalderen" means "the Middle Ages", the long stretch of European history before the modern age. In longer words, middelalder- means medieval: en middelalderby (a medieval town).

sentence.da: I **middelalderen** boede de fleste danskere på landet og dyrkede jorden.
sentence.en: In the Middle Ages most Danes lived in the countryside and farmed the land.

midlertidig.explanation: "Midlertidig" means "temporary", in place only for a short while: en midlertidig adresse (a temporary address).

sentence.da: Broen er **midlertidig**, fordi den nye bro ikke er færdig.
sentence.en: The bridge is temporary because the new bridge is not finished.

midnat.explanation: "Midnat" means "midnight", twelve o'clock at night. Do not mix it up with middag, which means noon or dinner.

sentence.da: Festen slutter først ved **midnat**.
sentence.en: The party only ends at midnight.

midt.explanation: "Midt" means "in the middle". It usually comes with i (in) or på (on): midt i byen (in the middle of town), midt på dagen (in the middle of the day).

forms.en: in the middle of the room
in the middle of the night

sentence.da: Der står et træ **midt** i haven.
sentence.en: There is a tree in the middle of the garden.

mig.explanation: "Mig" means "me". Compare Jeg ser ham (I see him) with Han ser mig (He sees me). It also comes after little words: til mig (to me), med mig (with me). With some verbs it means "myself": Jeg vasker mig (I wash myself).

sentence.da: Min ven giver **mig** en gave.
sentence.en: My friend gives me a gift.

mild.explanation: "Mild" means "mild", not sharp or extreme. It works for food and for weather: Vinteren er mild i år (The winter is mild this year).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have en **mild** sauce uden chili.
sentence.en: I want a mild sauce without chili.

militær.explanation: "Militær" means "military", about the armed forces: en militær base (a military base). The same word is used for the armed forces themselves: Han er i militæret (He is in the military).

sentence.da: Soldaterne træner på en **militær** base uden for byen.
sentence.en: The soldiers train at a military base outside the town.

million.explanation: "En million" means "a million". The thing you count comes after it: to millioner mennesker (two million people). Do not mix it up with en milliard, which means a billion (1,000 million).

sentence.da: Han vandt en **million** kroner i lotteriet.
sentence.en: He won a million kroner in the lottery.

min.explanation: "Min" means "my" or "mine" and is used with en-words. For et-words, use mit (my), as in mit hus (my house), and for several things use mine, as in mine børn (my children).

sentence.da: Jeg har en bil. **Min** bil er rød.
sentence.en: I have a car. My car is red.

mindre.explanation: "Mindre" means both less (an amount) and smaller (a size): mindre kaffe (less coffee), et mindre hus (a smaller house).

sentence.da: Et lille hus er **mindre** end et stort.
sentence.en: A small house is smaller than a big one.

mindst.explanation: "Mindst" means "least" and also "at least": Hvem har mindst tid? (Who has the least time?) With a number it sets the lowest amount: mindst fem (at least five).

forms.en: I will wait at least an hour

sentence.da: Du skal sove **mindst** otte timer.
sentence.en: You should sleep at least eight hours.

mine.explanation: "Mine" means "my" or "mine" when there is more than one thing. Compare min bog (my book) with mine bøger (my books), and mit hus (my house) with mine huse (my houses). It also works alone: Bøgerne er mine (The books are mine).

sentence.da: **Mine** børn hedder Peter og Anna.
sentence.en: My children are called Peter and Anna.

minigolf.explanation: "Minigolf" means "mini golf", the small golf game with fun obstacles.

sentence.da: I **minigolf** slår man bolden gennem en lille tunnel.
sentence.en: In mini golf, you hit the ball through a small tunnel.

minimal.explanation: "Minimal" means "minimal", the smallest amount possible or needed: en minimal forskel (a minimal difference).

sentence.da: Risikoen for fejl er **minimal**, fordi alt bliver tjekket to gange.
sentence.en: The risk of errors is minimal because everything is checked twice.

misfornøjet.explanation: "Misfornøjet" means "dissatisfied", unhappy because something is not as you hoped: misfornøjede medarbejdere (dissatisfied employees). The start mis- gives the idea of something wrong or bad, as in at misforstå (to misunderstand).

sentence.da: Kunden var **misfornøjet**, fordi maden kom for sent.
sentence.en: The customer was dissatisfied because the food came too late.

misforstået.explanation: "Misforstået" means "misunderstood", for a person or an idea that others do not see correctly: et misforstået geni (a misunderstood genius). It can also mean "misguided": misforstået loyalitet (misguided loyalty).

sentence.da: Hendes joke blev **misforstået**, så hun forklarede den igen.
sentence.en: Her joke was misunderstood, so she explained it again.

misinformation.explanation: "En misinformation" means "misinformation", false information that is passed on, often by people who believe it is true.

sentence.da: **Misinformation** spredes hurtigt på sociale medier, selv når folk mener det godt.
sentence.en: Misinformation spreads quickly on social media, even when people mean well.

mistillid.explanation: "En mistillid" means "distrust", the feeling that someone cannot be trusted. It is the opposite of tillid (trust), and in politics a mistillidsvotum is a vote of no confidence.

sentence.da: Der er stor **mistillid** mellem de to lande efter krigen.
sentence.en: There is great distrust between the two countries after the war.

mistænkelig.explanation: "Mistænkelig" means "suspicious", for something that looks wrong and makes others distrust it: en mistænkelig lyd (a suspicious sound). A person who feels distrust toward others is mistænksom, a different word.

sentence.da: Manden virkede **mistænkelig**, fordi han skjulte sit ansigt.
sentence.en: The man seemed suspicious because he hid his face.

mistænksom.explanation: "Mistænksom" means "suspicious", for a person who does not trust others easily: en mistænksom nabo (a suspicious neighbor). Something that looks wrong is mistænkelig, a different word.

sentence.da: Hunden er **mistænksom** over for fremmede, og den gøer højt.
sentence.en: The dog is suspicious of strangers, and it barks loudly.

mistænkt.explanation: "Mistænkt" means "suspected", for someone or something thought to be behind a crime or a problem: et mistænkt tilfælde (a suspected case). As a person word, en mistænkt is a suspect.

sentence.da: Manden er **mistænkt** for tyveriet, men han nægter.
sentence.en: The man is suspected of the theft, but he denies it.

misundelig.explanation: "Misundelig" means "envious", wanting what someone else has. Add på (of) and the person: Han er misundelig på sin kollega (He is envious of his coworker).

sentence.da: Jeg er **misundelig** på din nye bil.
sentence.en: I am envious of your new car.

misundelse.explanation: "En misundelse" means "envy", the unhappy feeling when someone else has something you want. The word for fear of losing someone's love to another person is jalousi (jealousy).

sentence.da: Hun følte **misundelse**, da veninden fik et drømmejob.
sentence.en: She felt envy when her friend got a dream job.

misvisende.explanation: "Misvisende" means "misleading", giving a false picture of something. It is often said about headlines, figures and information.

sentence.da: Overskriften er **misvisende**, fordi artiklen siger noget andet.
sentence.en: The headline is misleading because the article says something else.

mit.explanation: "Mit" means "my" or "mine" for words that go with et. Compare mit hus (my house, because et hus) with min bil (my car, because en bil), and mine huse (my houses, more than one). It also works alone: Huset er mit (The house is mine).

sentence.da: Jeg har et hus. **Mit** hus er gult.
sentence.en: I have a house. My house is yellow.

mod.explanation: "Mod" means "toward" and also "against". Compare Han går mod døren (He walks toward the door) with Vi spiller mod Sverige (We play against Sweden). To say you are against an idea, use imod: Jeg er imod det (I am against it).

sentence.da: Vi går **mod** stationen.
sentence.en: We are walking toward the station.

mode.explanation: "Mode" means "fashion", the clothes and styles people like now. Don't confuse it with måde (way), as in en god måde (a good way).

sentence.da: Min søster elsker **mode** og køber meget tøj.
sentence.en: My sister loves fashion and buys a lot of clothes.

moderigtig.explanation: "Moderigtig" means "fashionable", in line with what is in style right now. It is built from mode (fashion) and rigtig (right), so it is literally "right for the fashion".

sentence.da: Den jakke er **moderigtig** nu, men måske ikke næste år.
sentence.en: That jacket is fashionable now, but maybe not next year.

moderne.explanation: "Moderne" means "modern", for things that are up to date, such as styles and art: moderne kunst (modern art). The opposite is gammeldags (old-fashioned).

sentence.da: Vi bor i et **moderne** hus med store vinduer.
sentence.en: We live in a modern house with big windows.

modgang.explanation: "En modgang" means "adversity", a period when things go badly and life is hard. It is the opposite of medgang (good fortune), and the two appear together in i medgang og modgang (in good times and bad).

sentence.da: Gode venner står ved din side, når du har **modgang**.
sentence.en: Good friends stand by your side when you face adversity.

modig.explanation: "Modig" means "brave" and describes someone who is not afraid of hard or scary things. The opposite is bange (scared).

sentence.da: Hun er **modig** og tør tale foran hundrede mennesker.
sentence.en: She is brave and dares to speak in front of a hundred people.

modløs.explanation: "Modløs" means "discouraged", having lost heart and the will to keep trying. It is built from mod (courage) and -løs (without), so it is literally without courage.

sentence.da: Efter det dårlige resultat blev hun **modløs** og ville give op.
sentence.en: After the bad result she became discouraged and wanted to give up.

modsat.explanation: "Modsat" means "opposite", the other way around: Før er det modsatte af efter (Before is the opposite of after).

sentence.da: Han gik til højre, og jeg gik i **modsat** retning.
sentence.en: He went right, and I went in the opposite direction.

modstandsdygtig.explanation: "Modstandsdygtig" means "resilient", able to resist harm such as illness, cold or stress, for people, plants and materials. It is built from modstand (resistance) and dygtig (skilled).

sentence.da: Planten er **modstandsdygtig** og klarer sig godt i frost.
sentence.en: The plant is resilient and does well in frost.

moms.explanation: "Moms" means "VAT" or "sales tax", the tax that is added to prices in shops. To ask about it, say: Er det med moms? (Is VAT included?)

sentence.da: Prisen er tusind kroner med **moms**.
sentence.en: The price is a thousand kroner with VAT.

moralsk.explanation: "Moralsk" means "moral", about what people feel is right and wrong, not about what the law says.

sentence.da: Er det forkert at lyve? Det er et **moralsk** spørgsmål.
sentence.en: Is it wrong to lie? That is a moral question.

morgenmad.explanation: "Morgenmad" means "breakfast". It is morgen (morning) and mad (food) joined together. No a is needed: Jeg spiser morgenmad (I eat breakfast).

sentence.da: Om morgenen spiser jeg **morgenmad**: brød og kaffe.
sentence.en: In the morning I eat breakfast: bread and coffee.

morsom.explanation: "Morsom" means "funny" in a light, amusing way. In everyday speech, many people say sjov (fun) instead: en sjov fyr (a fun guy).

sentence.da: Han er **morsom** og får alle til at le.
sentence.en: He is funny and makes everyone laugh.

mos.explanation: "Et mos" means both "moss", the soft green plant that grows on stones and trees, and "mash", food mashed soft. The other words in the sentence show which one is meant.

sentence.da: Der vokser **mos** på de gamle sten.
sentence.en: Moss grows on the old stones.

motion.explanation: "Motion" means "exercise", physical activity that is good for you. For a single exercise in a lesson, use en øvelse (an exercise): en øvelse i grammatik (a grammar exercise).

sentence.da: Jeg går en lang tur for at få **motion**.
sentence.en: I take a long walk to get exercise.

motivation.explanation: "Motivation" means "motivation", the drive that makes you want to do something.

sentence.da: Jeg har ingen **motivation** til at træne.
sentence.en: I have no motivation to exercise.

mozzarella.explanation: "Mozzarella" means "mozzarella", a soft, mild Italian cheese that melts well.

sentence.da: Til salaten køber jeg frisk **mozzarella** og tomater.
sentence.en: For the salad, I buy fresh mozzarella and tomatoes.

mudder.explanation: "Et mudder" means "mud", wet, soft earth that sticks to your shoes and sinks under your feet. It is used for the mud itself and has no plural.

sentence.da: Efter regnen var marken fuld af **mudder**.
sentence.en: After the rain the field was full of mud.

mulig.explanation: "Mulig" means "possible": Det er muligt (It is possible). It is also in a useful set phrase: så hurtigt som muligt (as fast as possible).

sentence.da: Regn er **mulig** i morgen, men ikke sikker.
sentence.en: Rain is possible tomorrow, but not certain.

muligvis.explanation: "Muligvis" means "possibly" and is built from mulig (possible): Hun er muligvis syg (She is possibly sick). It can also answer a question: Kommer hun? Muligvis. (Is she coming? Possibly.)

sentence.da: Vi tager **muligvis** til Spanien i sommer.
sentence.en: We are possibly going to Spain this summer.

mundtlig.explanation: "Mundtlig" means "oral" or "spoken", done by speaking and not by writing. It comes from en mund (a mouth), so it is literally "of the mouth".

sentence.da: Jeg skal ikke skrive, fordi eksamen er **mundtlig**.
sentence.en: I do not have to write because the exam is oral.

munter.explanation: "Munter" means "cheerful", in a bright mood full of energy. It describes how someone acts and sounds, such as a laugh or a voice, more than a deep feeling.

sentence.da: Hun var **munter** og sang hele vejen hjem.
sentence.en: She was cheerful and sang all the way home.

musik.explanation: "Musik" means "music". It is used without en or "et": Jeg elsker musik (I love music). For a school lesson, Jeg har musik means "I have music class".

sentence.da: Jeg lytter gerne til **musik**.
sentence.en: I like listening to music.

musikalsk.explanation: "Musikalsk" means "musical", like having a talent for music. It can describe a whole group of people too: en musikalsk familie (a musical family).

sentence.da: Min datter er meget **musikalsk** og elsker at synge.
sentence.en: My daughter is very musical and loves to sing.

muskuløs.explanation: "Muskuløs" means "muscular", with big muscles you can see. It is about how a body looks, so a person can be stærk (strong) without being muskuløs.

sentence.da: Gymnasten er **muskuløs**, fordi han træner hver dag.
sentence.en: The gymnast is muscular because he trains every day.

muslimsk.explanation: "Muslimsk" means "Muslim" and describes things linked to that faith. A person is en muslim (a Muslim), while muslimsk is used for things such as customs, food and prayer.

sentence.da: Ramadanen er en **muslimsk** tradition.
sentence.en: Ramadan is a Muslim tradition.

mystisk.explanation: "Mystisk" means "mysterious", strange and hard to explain. Mærkelig (strange) only says something is odd, but mystisk also hints that there is something behind it.

sentence.da: Der står en **mystisk** mand uden for vores dør.
sentence.en: A mysterious man is standing outside our door.

mytologi.explanation: "En mytologi" means "mythology", the old stories about gods and heroes that a people once believed in.

sentence.da: Thor er en figur i den nordiske **mytologi**.
sentence.en: Thor is a figure in Norse mythology.

må jeg bede om regningen?.explanation: "Må jeg bede om regningen?" means "May I have the bill?" and is a polite way to ask for it at a restaurant. Må jeg bede om means "may I ask for". A shorter everyday way is Regningen, tak (The bill, please).

sentence.da: Vi har spist. **Må jeg bede om regningen?**
sentence.en: We have eaten. May I have the bill?

må jeg få regningen?.explanation: "Må jeg få regningen?" means "May I have the bill?" Må jeg få works for anything you ask for politely: after it, just say what you want.

forms.da: Må jeg få en kop kaffe?
forms.en: May I have a cup of coffee?

related.en: May I have the bill? (more formal)

sentence.da: Maden var god. **Må jeg få regningen?**
sentence.en: The food was good. May I have the bill?

målrettet.explanation: "Målrettet" means "goal-oriented", working steadily toward a clear goal without getting distracted. It is built from et mål (a goal) and rettet (aimed), and it is a positive word for people, work and plans.

sentence.da: Hun er **målrettet** og ved præcis, hvad hun vil.
sentence.en: She is goal-oriented and knows exactly what she wants.

månedsvis.explanation: "Månedsvis" means "for months", used when something goes on for a long time counted in months. It is built from en måned (a month) and -vis, which turns a unit of time into "for ... at a time".

sentence.da: Vi ventede **månedsvis** på svar fra kommunen.
sentence.en: We waited for months for an answer from the municipality.

måske.explanation: "Måske" means "maybe" or "perhaps". Compare Kommer du? Ja! (Are you coming? Yes!) with Kommer du? Måske. (Are you coming? Maybe). It can also start a sentence: Måske regner det i morgen (Maybe it will rain tomorrow).

sentence.da: **Måske** kommer han i morgen.
sentence.en: Maybe he will come tomorrow.

mægtig.explanation: "Mægtig" means "mighty" or "powerful", for rulers and nations with great strength, and for things big enough to impress. In everyday speech, it can also mean "really" before another word: mægtig flot (really nice).

sentence.da: Ørnen er en **mægtig** fugl med store vinger.
sentence.en: The eagle is a mighty bird with large wings.

mælk.explanation: "Mælk" means "milk": Jeg drikker mælk (I drink milk). To count it, use a measure: en liter mælk (a liter of milk).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker et glas **mælk** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I drink a glass of milk every morning.

mærkbar.explanation: "Mærkbar" means "noticeable", big enough that you can feel or see it. It is built from at mærke (to notice) and -bar (can be), so it literally means "can be noticed". It is used when something changes clearly, such as a price or a temperature.

sentence.da: Forskellen er **mærkbar**, og alle kan se den.
sentence.en: The difference is noticeable and everyone can see it.

mærkelig.explanation: "Mærkelig" means "strange", something odd that stands out. It is built from at mærke (to notice), and et mærke (a brand, a mark) is from the same family: et dyrt mærke (an expensive brand).

sentence.da: Der er en **mærkelig** lyd i køkkenet.
sentence.en: There is a strange sound in the kitchen.

mæt.explanation: "Mæt" means "full" after eating: Jeg er mæt (I am full) is a polite way to turn down more food. Do not use fuld after a meal: Jeg er fuld means "I am drunk".

sentence.da: Jeg har spist meget og er **mæt**.
sentence.en: I have eaten a lot and am full.

mættende.explanation: "Mættende" means "filling", said about food that keeps you from getting hungry again soon.

sentence.da: Havregrød er **mættende**, og man bliver ikke hurtigt sulten.
sentence.en: Oatmeal is filling and you do not get hungry quickly.

møbleret.explanation: "Møbleret" means "furnished", for a room or apartment that comes with furniture. Without furniture, say umøbleret (unfurnished).

sentence.da: Værelset er **møbleret** med seng, bord og stol.
sentence.en: The room is furnished with a bed, table and chair.

mør.explanation: "Mør" means "tender", for meat or other food that is soft and easy to cut or chew. The opposite is sej (tough): Kødet er sejt (The meat is tough).

sentence.da: Kødet er **mør**, fordi det har stået længe i ovnen.
sentence.en: The meat is tender because it has been in the oven a long time.

mørk.explanation: "Mørk" means "dark", for places with little light and for deep colors. It also goes in front of a color to make it deeper: mørkeblå (dark blue).

sentence.da: Om natten er himlen **mørk**.
sentence.en: At night the sky is dark.

mørke.explanation: "Mørke" means "darkness", the lack of light. To describe something dark, use mørk: et mørkt rum (a dark room).

sentence.da: Vi sidder i **mørke**, når strømmen går.
sentence.en: We sit in the dark when the power goes out.

mørkeblå.explanation: "Mørkeblå" means "dark blue" or "navy". It is built from mørk (dark) and blå (blue). A bright blue like a clear sky is himmelblå (sky blue).

sentence.da: Himlen er **mørkeblå** før solopgang.
sentence.en: The sky is dark blue before sunrise.

mørkegrøn.explanation: "Mørkegrøn" means "dark green". It is built from mørk (dark) and grøn (green). A fresh green like grass is græsgrøn (grass green).

sentence.da: Granen er **mørkegrøn** hele året.
sentence.en: The fir tree is dark green all year.

mørketid.explanation: "En mørketid" means "a dark season", the time of year with very short days and little daylight. In the far north, the sun does not rise at all for weeks.

sentence.da: I årets **mørketid** er dagene meget korte.
sentence.en: In the dark season of the year the days are very short.

mørkhåret.explanation: "Mørkhåret" means "dark-haired", with dark hair, usually brown or black. It is built from mørk (dark), hår (hair) and the ending -et, a pattern Danes use to describe how someone looks.

sentence.da: Han er høj og **mørkhåret**, og han har blå øjne.
sentence.en: He is tall and dark-haired, and he has blue eyes.

müsli.explanation: "Müsli" means "muesli", the breakfast mix of grains, nuts and dried fruit.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser **müsli** med mælk i en skål.
sentence.en: I eat muesli with milk in a bowl.
